summary: Anonymous non-place ARC rvalues are materialized as scope-owned temporaries so discarded results and borrowed call arguments remain live through consumption and are then released.
evidence_paraphrase: The chosen helper emits a fresh typed temporary, registers it as owned in the current scope, and relies on scope-exit cleanup.
alternatives: Leave anonymous ARC results unmanaged | Insert ad hoc immediate releases at each expression form
rationale: Scope-owned materialization gives ARC temporaries one uniform lifetime rule across discarded expressions and nested calls.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the ARC ownership ADRs.

summary: A borrowed ARC parameter was promoted lazily to an owned binding on its first reassignment, without releasing the caller-owned old value, and ownership was registered in the declaring function scope.
evidence_section: Fix param reassignment of borrowed ARC values
evidence_paraphrase: The plan says to skip cleanup of the borrowed old value, promote the parameter in its declaring scope, and use normal owned replacement thereafter.
alternatives: Retain reassigned ARC parameters at function entry | Reject ARC parameter reassignment
rationale: Lazy promotion sought to avoid touching the caller's borrow and to pay ownership cost only once reassignment occurred.
adr_recommendation: Historical rule is documented through the ARC ADR's related-plan chain; no separate ADR.

summary: The Stage 2 parser is a behavior-preserving port whose grammar, parse structure, and equivalent diagnostic codes follow Stage 1.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan directs Stage 2 to keep the Stage 1 recursive-descent shape, preserve equivalent PAR codes, and remain syntax-only.
alternatives: Design an independently structured Stage 2 parser | Permit Stage 2 grammar or diagnostic divergence
rationale: A mechanical oracle relationship reduces bootstrap divergence and makes Stage 1 behavior the reviewable reference.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the Dea-wide two-stage architecture ADR.

summary: Stage 2 uses a hybrid AST: declaration/shared metadata is pointer-owned, while expressions, statements, and patterns are arena-backed and connected by integer IDs.
evidence_section: Chosen AST Storage Model: Hybrid Arena
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly selects pointer-owned metadata plus arena-backed high-volume graph nodes addressed by stable integer handles.
alternatives: Fully pointer-linked AST | Fully arena-backed AST including declaration metadata
rationale: The split keeps dense parse graphs contiguous and ownership-safe while leaving declaration metadata easy to construct and manipulate.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: Stage 2 arena-backed AST and ownership model.

summary: The parser is a syntax-only phase; semantic and type-checking logic stays outside it.
evidence_paraphrase: The porting policy explicitly excludes semantic and type-checking logic from the parser.
alternatives: Perform name or type resolution during parsing
rationale: A syntax-only parser preserves explicit compiler phase boundaries and avoids semantic coupling in recovery paths.
adr_recommendation: Stable architecture documentation is sufficient for this conventional phase boundary.

summary: A Stage 2 ParseResult owns its module and AST arenas, and the caller releases the aggregate with parse_result_free.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan defines parser-returned ownership of the module and arenas and one aggregate caller-side free operation.
alternatives: Caller-owned individual AST allocations | Parser-global lifetime with no explicit result cleanup
rationale: Aggregate ownership gives later passes stable AST handles and one deterministic cleanup boundary.
adr_recommendation: Document as an internal parser API contract; a standalone ADR is not necessary.

summary: Trace analysis fails only for definite runtime faults; suspicious or compatibility heuristics remain warnings.
evidence_paraphrase: The failure policy is explicitly definite-issues-only, while suspicious cases are non-fatal warnings.
alternatives: Fail on every suspicious trace pattern | Never fail and report findings only
rationale: The checker can act as a CI gate without turning uncertain heuristics into false failures.
adr_recommendation: Keep this policy in the tool and trace documentation; no ADR is needed.

summary: Inline `with` cleanup is registered after each successful header item, so a later `?` short-circuit runs only prior completed cleanups in LIFO order.
secondary_categories: Ownership and memory safety | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: Header items are emitted in order and each successful item's cleanup is prepended immediately, preserving LIFO behavior on later short-circuit.
alternatives: Register all cleanups before any header initialization | Skip all cleanup when a header initializer short-circuits
rationale: Only resources actually acquired before the failure may be cleaned, and cleanup order must reverse acquisition order.

summary: A cleanup block may not reference a non-nullable `with` header binding that can be uninitialized on a `?` header-failure path.
evidence_section: Type safety guard for cleanup-block references
evidence_paraphrase: The type checker marks affected header lets as maybe-uninitialized and rejects cleanup references to non-nullable ones with TYP-0156.
alternatives: Permit the reference and synthesize a hidden sentinel | Ban all cleanup references when any header can short-circuit
rationale: The rule preserves non-nullability without unnecessarily rejecting safely nullable or unrelated cleanup bindings.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: The broader `with` ADR plus normative grammar and diagnostic catalog are sufficient.

summary: `module parser` remains the sole stable public import facade while expression, statement, declaration, and shared parser internals live in private submodules.
evidence_paraphrase: The refactor preserves the external `import parser` contract exactly and moves internals behind parser submodules.
alternatives: Expose each parser submodule to callers | Keep the parser monolithic
rationale: A facade preserves callers while allowing internal decomposition without import cycles or API churn.
adr_recommendation: An internal module-facade contract does not require a standalone ADR.

summary: The Stage 2 parser's public result API exposed a single ParseError/ParseErrorState alongside ParseResult.
evidence_paraphrase: The preserved public facade explicitly includes ParseError, ParseErrorState, ParseResult, and conversion from private single-error state.
alternatives: Expose only a diagnostic collection | Raise or abort on the first parse error
rationale: At that point the stable facade mirrored the existing single-error parser result while internals were split.
adr_recommendation: Historical internal API; the later diagnostics-only result requires no separate ADR beyond the plan chain.

summary: Compiler operating modes are selected by global flags rather than subcommand words.

alternatives: Retain argparse subcommands | Support both forms as equally canonical

adr_recommendation: Covered by the shared CLI ADR.

summary: `--build` is the compiler's default mode when no primary mode flag is supplied.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly selects build as the omitted-mode default.

rationale: Build preserves the compiler-driver default expected for ordinary invocations.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the shared CLI ADR.

summary: Stage 1 initially retained a compatibility shim that rewrote the first recognized legacy command word into a mode flag.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly keeps a simple command-word-to-mode-flag compatibility rewrite.
alternatives: Make the mode-flag migration a hard cut | Keep subcommands as the primary syntax

summary: Runtime arguments for `--run` must follow a `--` separator, and the separator is invalid outside run mode.

summary: A compiler invocation accepts exactly one source target; multi-target execution remains outside the current contract.

adr_recommendation: Covered by the shared CLI ADR.

summary: The initial short-option allocation kept `-I` for `--runtime-include`.

rationale: The choice preserved the then-existing L0 runtime-include spelling.

summary: `--include-eof` is a long-only token-dump option.

adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the shared CLI contract and ADR.

summary: Mode-scoped options are validated as fatal CLI errors when used with incompatible modes.

alternatives: Silently ignore incompatible options | Accept every option globally and defer failure
rationale: Early validation gives deterministic behavior and prevents flags from being silently ineffective.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the shared CLI ADR.

summary: With `--run --keep-c`, generated C is retained as `./a.c` by default or as `<output>.c` when `-o` is supplied, while the executable remains temporary.

adr_recommendation: Covered by the shared CLI contract; no separate ADR.

summary: The Stage 2 CLI accepts mode flags only and deliberately omits the Stage 1 legacy command-word rewrite shim.
evidence_paraphrase: The first locked decision makes Stage 2 flags-only and expressly rejects a legacy command-word shim.

summary: `L0_HOME` denotes the compiler root, from which the default stdlib and runtime include paths are derived under `shared/`.

adr_recommendation: Covered by the shared CLI/environment contract.

summary: Stage 2 lexer and parser diagnostics use the common `util.diag` Diagnostic/DiagCollector representation.

summary: The Stage 2 lexer remained fail-fast at the first lexer error even after adopting Diagnostic records.

rationale: The refactor initially limited behavior change while unifying the diagnostic API.

summary: The Stage 2 parser public result is diagnostics-only, with a collector and helper queries instead of a public single-error enum.

adr_recommendation: Keep as a stable parser API contract; no standalone ADR is necessary.

summary: Parser recovery was initially limited to synchronization between top-level declarations, with no statement-level recovery.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan chooses top-level synchronization only and explicitly excludes deep statement-level recovery.

rationale: A narrow recovery boundary reduced semantic drift while enabling multiple top-level diagnostics.
adr_recommendation: Historical recovery limit was broadened by later parser-recovery plans; no ADR needed.

summary: Source-entry parsing initially copied lexer diagnostics directly into the ParseResult diagnostic collector.
evidence_paraphrase: The lex-to-parse path is directed to propagate the lexer's collector entries into the parse result.

rationale: Direct propagation gave callers one result surface before logical recovery tokens existed.
adr_recommendation: Superseded by the logical lexer-error wrapper-token ADR.

summary: Reusable containers and text infrastructure are public flat `std.*` modules shared by both L0 compiler stages rather than Stage 2-private `util.*` modules.

adr_recommendation: Covered by the stdlib module-boundary ADR.

summary: Compiler-specific diagnostic infrastructure remains private to Stage 2 as `util.diag` and is not promoted to `std.diag`.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly adds no std.diag module while lifting reusable data structures and text helpers.
alternatives: Expose diagnostics as a general stdlib module | Move diagnostics into another public support namespace
rationale: The diagnostic model is compiler-specific rather than a general L0 program API.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: The stdlib boundary ADR is sufficient.

summary: The L0 stdlib dependency graph must remain acyclic, specifically avoiding mutual imports between `std.string` and `std.text`.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan requires an acyclic final graph and forbids forcing a std.string/std.text import cycle.
alternatives: Permit mutually recursive stdlib modules | Break cycles through compiler-specific import exceptions
rationale: Acyclic stdlib modules keep bootstrap loading deterministic and avoid special module-cycle semantics.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Treat as a consequence of the stdlib module-boundary ADR.

summary: String construction, case conversion, repetition, reversal, and integer formatting helpers remain in `std.text` rather than moving to `std.string`.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan expressly keeps concat, case, repeat, reverse, and integer-formatting helpers in std.text.
alternatives: Move all string-returning helpers into `std.string` | Split formatting into a separate module
rationale: Keeping higher-level text assembly and formatting together preserves the acyclic low-level string/text boundary.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the stdlib module-boundary ADR.

summary: Unwrapping a place-owned `string?` with `opt as string` is non-consuming: the optional remains valid and the value is ownership-stabilized only when it crosses a real ownership boundary.
secondary_categories: Language semantics | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: The plan states that unwrap is not move-out, does not invalidate the optional, and should gain ownership only at actual ownership boundaries rather than through blanket retains.
alternatives: Treat unwrap as a move that consumes the optional | Retain every unwrap result immediately
rationale: Non-consuming value semantics preserve the source optional while avoiding both dangling aliases and unnecessary retains.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the ARC and nullability ADRs plus the normative ownership section.

summary: L0 I/O wrappers classify success and failure solely from each runtime call's direct return value, never from ambient `errno`.
evidence_paraphrase: Each affected wrapper's failure rule is defined by null, false, or -1 from the called runtime function, with errno removed from classification.
alternatives: Require both a failure return and nonzero errno | Clear and inspect errno around every wrapper call
rationale: Process-global errno can be stale; the called function's explicit return channel is the only operation-specific evidence.
adr_recommendation: A narrow, obvious error-channel correction is fully represented in stable stdlib documentation.

summary: Mixed `int`/`byte` relational and equality expressions remain valid numeric operations; the backend must lower them rather than reject them as a type mismatch.
secondary_categories: Backend and C emission | Language semantics
evidence_paraphrase: The plan deliberately keeps the type checker's mixed numeric semantics unchanged and aligns backend comparison/equality lowering with them.
alternatives: Tighten the type checker to require equal operand types | Require explicit casts between int and byte
rationale: The two fixed-width integer types are intentionally compatible in numeric contexts, and backend rejection would contradict accepted source semantics.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: numeric compatibility, result types, and promotion rules for `int` and `byte`.

summary: Bindings declared in a `with` header remain in scope throughout all inline and block cleanup clauses.
secondary_categories: Type system | Ownership and memory safety
evidence_paraphrase: The plan states that header variables remain scoped for the duration of every cleanup clause.
alternatives: Scope each binding only to its own cleanup | Expose header bindings to the body but not cleanup clauses
rationale: Cleanup must be able to release or inspect resources acquired in the header, including during LIFO unwinding.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Clarify explicitly in the existing `with` ADR or normative grammar; no new ADR.

summary: Parsing and formatting conversions live in `std.text`, while low-level character, byte, and raw string helpers remain in `std.string`.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly assigns conversion/parsing APIs to std.text and low-level byte/string character helpers to std.string.
alternatives: Keep integer parsing in `std.string` | Place conversions in per-type modules
rationale: The split distinguishes raw byte-string operations from textual representation and parsing.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the stdlib module-boundary ADR.

summary: The canonical boolean text representation is lowercase `true`/`false`; parsing is case-sensitive and returns null for every other spelling.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan accepts exactly lowercase true and false and specifies null for other input.
alternatives: Case-insensitive parsing | Accept numeric or abbreviated boolean spellings | Panic on invalid text
rationale: One strict representation avoids locale and synonym ambiguity while using optionals for parse failure.
adr_recommendation: Narrow public helper semantics are adequately normative in the stdlib reference.

summary: `std.string::byte_to_s` remains a one-character byte conversion, while numeric byte formatting and parsing use distinct explicit `std.text` APIs.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan preserves character-byte conversion and separates it from numeric byte conversion by name and module.
alternatives: Make byte_to_s format a decimal number | Overload one conversion name by context
rationale: A byte can denote either a character code unit or a number; distinct APIs prevent contextual ambiguity.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: The stdlib boundary ADR plus API reference is sufficient.

summary: Numeric byte parsing validates the inclusive range 0 through 255 and returns null for invalid or out-of-range input rather than wrapping or saturating.
evidence_paraphrase: The parser reuses integer parsing, applies an explicit 0..255 range check, and returns null on failure.
alternatives: Wrap modulo 256 | Saturate to the nearest byte value | Panic on invalid input
rationale: Optional failure preserves the byte range invariant without silent numeric distortion.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: The fixed-width integer ADR and stdlib API reference are sufficient.

summary: Base-aware integer and byte text conversions support bases 2 through 16; invalid bases or invalid/overflowing parse input do not produce wrapped values.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan fixes the supported base interval at 2..16 and rejects invalid or out-of-range byte text with null.
alternatives: Support bases through 36 | Support only binary, decimal, and hexadecimal | Wrap on integer overflow
rationale: The restricted base alphabet matches the existing ASCII digit helpers and keeps bootstrap parsing small and deterministic.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Stable stdlib docs plus the integer ADR are sufficient.

summary: `split_s` accepts a string separator and preserves empty tokens between, before, or after matches.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects string separators and keep-empty split semantics.
alternatives: Split on one byte only | Drop empty tokens by default
rationale: String separators support compiler/text workloads and preserving empties avoids information loss.
adr_recommendation: Narrow stdlib helper semantics are fully represented in the API reference.

summary: Calling `split_s` with an empty separator is a runtime assertion failure.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan rejects an empty separator with a fixed assertion message.
alternatives: Split into individual bytes | Return the whole input unchanged | Return an optional failure
rationale: An empty substring has infinitely many match positions, so rejecting it avoids arbitrary semantics.
adr_recommendation: Keep in the stdlib API contract; no ADR.

summary: `lines_s` uses LF as the line delimiter and strips one trailing CR from each resulting line, normalizing CRLF input.
evidence_paraphrase: The selected line splitting policy is LF-based with per-line trailing CR removal.
alternatives: Preserve CR bytes | Recognize CR as an independent line delimiter
rationale: The policy gives the same logical lines for Unix LF and Windows CRLF text.
adr_recommendation: Narrow portable text-helper behavior belongs in the stdlib reference.

summary: `lines_s` maps an empty input string to an empty vector, not a vector containing one empty line.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly specifies zero lines for empty input.
alternatives: Return one empty line
rationale: No input characters and no line terminator represent no lines in this API.

summary: A trailing final LF does not create an additional empty element in `lines_s`.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly suppresses a final empty line caused solely by a terminal newline.
alternatives: Preserve a terminal empty line
rationale: The API treats a terminal newline as line termination rather than the start of another logical line.

summary: `replace_s` performs global non-overlapping replacement from left to right.
evidence_paraphrase: The replacement order and non-overlap rule are explicitly fixed.
alternatives: Allow overlapping matches | Replace only the first match | Choose right-to-left matches
rationale: Left-to-right non-overlap is deterministic and matches conventional string replacement behavior.

summary: Calling `replace_s` with an empty old pattern is a runtime assertion failure.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan rejects an empty old pattern with a fixed assertion message.
alternatives: Insert replacement at every boundary | Return the original string | Return an optional failure
rationale: Rejecting an empty pattern avoids ambiguous unbounded match-position semantics.

summary: The public `std.time` model distinguishes wall-clock snapshots, monotonic snapshots, durations, and calendar date-times as separate value types.
evidence_section: Public API Changes / Added module: std.time
evidence_paraphrase: The plan introduces distinct WallTime, MonotonicTime, Duration, and DateTime structures and operations.
alternatives: Represent all time concepts as bare integer seconds | Use one tagged universal time structure
rationale: Distinct types prevent accidental mixing of civil time, monotonic measurements, and elapsed duration.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: L0 time model and runtime boundary.

summary: Runtime clock snapshots use a single out-pointer call returning sec/nsec together, preventing torn readings across multiple calls.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects one runtime call per reading, backed by RtTimeParts out-pointer functions.
alternatives: Expose separate seconds and nanoseconds calls | Return only coarse integer seconds | Return a C struct by value
rationale: A one-call snapshot guarantees both components describe the same clock observation and keeps the FFI ABI simple.
adr_recommendation: Include in a P1 time-model ADR.

summary: Fallible public `std.time` operations return optionals/null rather than panicking or exposing sentinel values.
evidence_paraphrase: The public failure channel is explicitly optional null, not panic or sentinel.
alternatives: Panic on clock/conversion failure | Return sentinel time fields | Expose bool plus out-parameter publicly
rationale: Optionals make platform and conversion failure explicit in ordinary L0 control flow.
adr_recommendation: Include in a P1 time-model ADR.

summary: When a monotonic clock is unsupported, the API reports false/null and never substitutes wall-clock time.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly rejects a wall-clock fallback for unsupported monotonic clocks.
alternatives: Fall back transparently to wall time | Treat lack of monotonic support as a panic
rationale: A wall clock can jump and therefore cannot preserve monotonic duration semantics.
adr_recommendation: Include in a P1 time-model ADR.

summary: UTC civil-calendar conversion is implemented with integer-only date arithmetic in L0 rather than delegated to the C runtime.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan places UTC civil date math in L0 and restricts it to integer arithmetic.
alternatives: Delegate UTC conversion to libc `gmtime` | Expose raw Unix seconds only
rationale: Keeping deterministic UTC conversion in L0 avoids platform-specific libc representations and behavior.
adr_recommendation: Include in a P1 time-model ADR.

summary: Local calendar conversion delegates time-zone offset and DST lookup to the runtime at the source Unix second.
evidence_paraphrase: The selected runtime boundary supplies local UTC offset and DST metadata for the exact source second.
alternatives: Implement a time-zone database in L0 | Use the current offset regardless of source timestamp
rationale: Host facilities own local-zone policy, while querying at the source instant preserves historical DST correctness.
adr_recommendation: Include in a P1 time-model ADR.

summary: Nanosecond components are validated and normalized to the invariant `0 <= nsec < 1_000_000_000`.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan fixes the valid normalized nanosecond range.
alternatives: Permit unnormalized sec/nsec pairs | Clamp invalid nanoseconds
rationale: A canonical range makes comparison, subtraction, and calendar conversion deterministic.
adr_recommendation: Include in a P1 time-model ADR.

summary: The calendar model does not represent leap seconds; DateTime seconds remain in the range 0 through 59.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan expressly omits leap-second modeling and fixes the converted second range at 0..59.
alternatives: Allow second 60 for leap seconds | Represent leap-second state separately
rationale: POSIX-style Unix time and the bootstrap conversion algorithm do not carry leap-second information.
adr_recommendation: Include in a P1 time-model ADR.

summary: `drop` accepts both non-null and nullable pointers, and dropping null is a safe no-op.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan formalizes that nullable pointers can be dropped directly and null is handled as a no-op, making wrapper functions unnecessary.
alternatives: Reject nullable operands statically | Panic when a nullable operand contains null
rationale: Null-tolerant drop makes conditional acquisition cleanup direct and deterministic without helper wrappers.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the L0 ownership ADR and normative ownership documentation.

summary: ARC cleanup on loop exits is path-sensitive and releases only locals definitely initialized on the active path.
secondary_categories: Backend and C emission | Language semantics
evidence_paraphrase: The plan requires cleanup only for definitely initialized locals and covers exits between multiple acquisitions.
alternatives: Initialize every ARC local at loop entry | Emit unconditional lexical-scope cleanup
rationale: Releasing an uninitialized slot is undefined C behavior, while skipping an acquired value leaks; cleanup must follow actual acquisition paths.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the ARC ADRs and current backend design.

summary: A `for`-loop `continue` cleans the current iteration body scope, then executes the update step, while preserving the outer header scope.

summary: A `for`-loop `break` cleans both the current body scope and the outer `for` header scope before leaving the loop.
secondary_categories: Language semantics | Backend and C emission

adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by ARC ADRs plus normative backend design.

summary: For `while` loops, both `continue` and `break` clean the current loop-body scope before transferring control.

alternatives: Give while break and continue different ownership boundaries | Defer body cleanup until loop termination
rationale: Unlike `for`, `while` has no separately owned header scope; both exits leave the current body lifetime.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by ARC ADRs plus normative backend design.

summary: A single owning `AnalysisResult` aggregate carries the DriverState, combined diagnostics, name environments, signatures, and local-scope environments.
secondary_categories: Frontend architecture | Ownership and memory safety
evidence_paraphrase: The plan defines AnalysisResult as owner of the compilation driver state and every semantic result table, with typed lookup and cleanup.
alternatives: Return independent pass results with separate lifetimes | Store semantic state globally
rationale: One aggregate gives downstream typing/backend phases a coherent lifetime and lookup surface.

summary: Module name resolution creates all module environments first, collects local declarations second, opens imports third, and aggregates diagnostics last.

summary: concat3_s and concat4_s are removed from the public L0 and L1 standard-library surface.

alternatives: Retain all concat wrappers

summary: concat_s remains the public binary string helper and the lowering target for string +.

summary: L0 release workflows assemble a draft completely before publication and never mutate a published release.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects a draft-first publication model covering stable releases, snapshots, and manual documentation assets, with published releases treated as immutable.
alternatives: Create a public release first and upload or replace assets afterward | Permit later workflow mutation of published releases
rationale: Publication occurs only after the complete artifact set is ready, avoiding partially published or subsequently mutated releases.
adr_recommendation: P1: create an L0 release-publication ADR covering immutable draft-first release assembly and its manual workflow boundary.

summary: SHA256SUMS covers every staged L0 release asset and records bare filenames without a ./ prefix.
evidence_paraphrase: Stable and snapshot workflows stage all release artifacts before publication, and the checksum manifest must enumerate every one using bare names.
alternatives: Checksum only platform archives | Record path-prefixed manifest entries
rationale: A complete, location-neutral checksum manifest makes the public artifact set independently verifiable after download.
adr_recommendation: Bundle into the proposed P1 L0 release-publication ADR as the artifact-integrity contract.

summary: Manual L0 snapshot dispatch supports a draft-only mode through publish_release=false.
evidence_paraphrase: The snapshot workflow deliberately retains a nonpublishing manual-dispatch mode.
alternatives: Every manual snapshot dispatch publishes immediately | Use a separate draft-only workflow
rationale: Maintainers can assemble and inspect a snapshot without crossing the public-release boundary.
adr_recommendation: Bundle into the proposed P1 L0 release-publication ADR; no standalone ADR is warranted.

summary: The L0 documentation-publication workflow remains manual-only and may attach release assets only to an existing draft.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan fixes both the manual trigger boundary and the draft-only target requirement for documentation assets.
alternatives: Automatically publish documentation assets | Allow attachment to published releases
rationale: Manual preparation can enrich a pending release without creating a second route that mutates public releases.
adr_recommendation: Bundle into the proposed P1 L0 release-publication ADR; no standalone ADR is warranted.

summary: Repository Python tooling is one root uv workspace with l0 and l1 as members, one shared .venv, and one root uv.lock.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan replaces two projects writing one environment with a root workspace, level members, and a single lock and environment.
alternatives: Independent level projects with separate environments and locks | Independent locks writing one shared environment
rationale: One solver and lockfile eliminate dependency churn and match uv's native workspace model.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the Dea-wide monorepo directory-structure ADR.

summary: Shared development and documentation dependency groups are owned once by the root pyproject rather than duplicated in level projects.
evidence_section: Approach / Phase 1 — Add root pyproject and reshape level pyprojects
evidence_paraphrase: The root project takes the union of dev/docs groups while level projects retain only their own project and pytest configuration.
alternatives: Keep duplicated dependency groups in each level | Create a third tooling project solely for shared development dependencies
rationale: Central ownership makes the single workspace lock authoritative while preserving level-specific test settings.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the root-workspace portion of ADR-0004 and current monorepo documentation.

summary: uv remains optional: make venv prefers uv but falls back to an existing environment or python -m venv plus pip.
evidence_paraphrase: The root command preserves the three-tier uv-to-pip fallback, explicitly making uv an accelerator rather than a hard prerequisite.
alternatives: Require uv for every developer and CI environment | Use pip only and remove the lock-based fast path
rationale: The repository gains one deterministic uv workspace without excluding environments where uv is unavailable.
adr_recommendation: Extend ADR-0004 to state that uv is optional and the pip fallback is a maintained portability contract; no new ADR is needed.

summary: The public Markdown API-reference release asset is named dea_l0_api_reference-<TAG>.tar.gz.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects a level-, purpose-, and tag-qualified archive filename matching the PDF artifact family.
alternatives: Keep blog-export.tar.gz | Use an unversioned dea_l0_api_reference.tar.gz release asset
rationale: The name identifies both artifact purpose and exact release in listings and downstream caches.
adr_recommendation: P1: include the stable public L0 release-asset naming family in an L0 distribution/release contract ADR.

summary: Raw pointer indexing is not part of the L0 language surface; all ptr[i] forms are rejected.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan requires every raw pointer base, including int*, byte*, and string*, to be rejected and states that L0 has no indexable type until future array work.
alternatives: Allow direct C-like indexing on non-null pointers | Permit pointer indexing only for selected pointee types
rationale: L0 deliberately omits pointer arithmetic and has no array type whose bounds or ownership could give indexing a safe contract.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the L0 pointer-model ADR.

summary: L0 retains postfix index syntax and EX_INDEX AST nodes, but semantic analysis rejects them because no current L0 type is indexable.
evidence_section: Approach / 3. Tighten the L0 docs; 4. Keep parser and AST surface unchanged
evidence_paraphrase: The parser continues building EX_INDEX and the type checker owns rejection, preserving the frontend shape for future array support.
alternatives: Reject bracket indexing in the parser | Remove EX_INDEX until arrays exist
rationale: Keeping a syntactic/AST form avoids another parser redesign when a safe indexable type is eventually introduced.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: The stable language exclusion is covered by ADR-0002; the preparatory AST placement is too implementation-specific for a standalone ADR.

summary: L0 uses the generic TYP-0212 invalid-base diagnostic for non-null indexing bases, including raw pointers, rather than creating a pointer-specific code.
evidence_section: Approach / 2. Align parser and type-checker diagnostics with the intended rule
evidence_paraphrase: The plan preserves TYP-0212 as the generic non-null invalid-base code and explicitly declines to split pointer and non-pointer cases.
alternatives: Allocate a dedicated L0 raw-pointer-index diagnostic | Reuse the L1 pointer-index diagnostic family
rationale: All non-null bases share one unsupported-indexing condition in L0, so a pointer-specific taxonomy would imply a semantic distinction the language does not have.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the shared diagnostic-catalog ADR and catalog; no standalone ADR is warranted.

summary: unsafe is reserved and prefixes L1 function declarations as unsafe func and unsafe extern func.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan fixes the prefix position for ordinary and extern unsafe function declarations.
alternatives: Place unsafe after func or extern | Use an attribute or block-level marker instead of a declaration modifier
rationale: A function-level prefix exposes the unchecked contract at the declaration boundary and composes with extern declarations.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the L1 unsafe-marker ADR.

summary: Unsafe function pointer types are spelled unsafe func(...) -> T.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects the unsafe prefix as part of function-type syntax.
alternatives: Attach unsafe to the pointer value rather than the function type | Represent unsafe only on declarations and erase it from function pointer syntax
rationale: The source type visibly preserves the raw-memory contract through indirect references.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the function-pointer and unsafe-marker ADRs.

summary: Safe and unsafe function pointer types are distinct and have no implicit conversion in either direction.
evidence_paraphrase: The unsafe bit participates in type identity and neither type implicitly converts to the other.
alternatives: Treat unsafe as documentation only and erase it from type identity | Allow a one-way implicit conversion
rationale: Strict type identity prevents an indirect function reference from silently losing or gaining its declared memory contract.

summary: The unsafe function marker is a contract/type annotation, not a call-site gate; safe code may call unsafe function values.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly permits calls from safe functions and rejects call-site enforcement for this design.
alternatives: Require an unsafe function or unsafe block at every call site | Reject calls to unsafe values from safe functions
rationale: The initial bootstrap surface records the contract in signatures without introducing a second unsafe-context mechanism.
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0010, which also records that future tightening remains possible.

summary: Ordinary pointer dereference and pointer field access remain valid in safe L1 code.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan preserves *p and p.field outside unsafe functions because no pointer-provenance distinction yet separates safe heap pointers from raw pointers.
alternatives: Gate every dereference and pointer field access on unsafe func | Introduce provenance-qualified pointer types before permitting safe dereference
rationale: Existing heap-object pointer use remains ergonomic while the marker is reserved for operations whose safety cannot be expressed by the current pointer model.

summary: Safe and unsafe function types share the same generated C function-pointer representation while remaining distinct in L1 analysis.
secondary_categories: Backend and C emission | Type system
evidence_section: Implementation Phases / Phase 3: Backend, stdlib, and docs
evidence_paraphrase: The C ABI representation is intentionally unchanged even though analysis and interfaces retain the unsafe distinction.
alternatives: Use different C typedef shapes for safe and unsafe functions | Erase the unsafe distinction before interface and link boundaries
rationale: The safety distinction is a language/LBI contract and need not alter the host C calling convention.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the function-pointer and LBI ADRs.

summary: sys.memory externs with unchecked caller-side raw-memory preconditions are marked unsafe, while allocation functions that establish storage remain plain externs.
evidence_section: Implementation Phases / Phase 3: Backend, stdlib, and docs
evidence_paraphrase: The plan assigns unsafe to raw buffer/memory operations with caller preconditions and deliberately leaves rt_alloc and rt_calloc plain.
alternatives: Mark every sys.memory extern unsafe | Leave all extern declarations plain and communicate hazards only in prose
rationale: The public signature distinguishes operations that create valid storage from those requiring the caller to prove raw-memory conditions.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the unsafe-marker ADR together with the normative stdlib inventory.

summary: Raw pointer indexing was temporarily left accepted without an unsafe-function gate until the dedicated finalization plan.
evidence_paraphrase: The marker tranche deliberately preserves the then-current pointer-index behavior and assigns the unsafe-context gate to a later plan.
alternatives: Gate pointer indexing in the marker plan | Reject pointer indexing entirely until finalization
rationale: The feature was split so marker/type plumbing landed before the operation that consumed the new unsafe context.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: The superseding unsafe-gated rule is covered by ADR-0010; no historical standalone ADR is warranted.

summary: The shared low-level raw-memory standard-library module is named sys.memory rather than sys.unsafe.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly selects sys.memory as the shared L0/L1 module identity.
alternatives: Retain sys.unsafe | Choose a different neutral module name such as sys.alloc
rationale: The name describes the module's responsibility while freeing unsafe for L1 language syntax.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the stdlib module-boundaries ADR.

summary: Renaming the source module does not rename its rt_* function surface or runtime C symbols.
evidence_paraphrase: The Dea-visible function spellings and runtime C symbols are held stable across the module-path rename.
alternatives: Rename the runtime API together with the source module | Version or alias both old and new C symbols
rationale: The source namespace can evolve without an unnecessary runtime ABI break.
adr_recommendation: The level ABI ADRs cover the stable rt_* boundary generally; no separate ADR is warranted for this rename boundary.

summary: The sys.unsafe to sys.memory change is a hard source rename with no compatibility shim module.
evidence_paraphrase: The old module identity is intentionally removed rather than retained as an alias because unsafe must become a keyword.
alternatives: Retain sys.unsafe as an alias | Support both paths for a deprecation period
rationale: A shim would keep the soon-reserved keyword valid as a module-path component and defeat the prerequisite rename.
adr_recommendation: P2: bundle this with the other May hard renames in a shared stdlib API compatibility and naming-policy ADR.

summary: Postfix ptr[i] is the L1 source form for raw pointer indexing.
secondary_categories: Language semantics | Ownership and memory safety
evidence_paraphrase: The plan keeps the existing postfix spelling as the raw-pointer operation rather than adding a new syntax.
alternatives: Reject raw pointer indexing from L1 | Introduce a distinct explicit intrinsic or pointer-arithmetic syntax
rationale: The familiar postfix form can be shared with safe arrays while type and context determine whether the operation is raw.

summary: Raw pointer indexing is accepted only inside an unsafe func body.
evidence_paraphrase: The accepted form includes an enclosing unsafe-function requirement, while ordinary dereference and field access remain outside that gate.
alternatives: Permit ptr[i] in safe functions | Require an expression-level unsafe block
rationale: The function signature makes the unprovable raw-memory range obligation visible at the contract boundary.

summary: A raw-index base must be a non-null T* whose pointee is sized and not void.
evidence_paraphrase: The pointer-index contract excludes nullable bases and unsized void pointees.
alternatives: Allow nullable bases with a runtime null check | Define indexing arithmetic for void*
rationale: Indexing requires an element size and a non-null base before any source-level element access can be meaningful.
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0010 and the diagnostic catalog.

summary: Raw pointer indexes must have type int.
evidence_paraphrase: The accepted pointer-index form fixes the index operand type to L1 int.
alternatives: Accept every integer-family type | Implicitly convert integral indexes to int
rationale: One index type keeps pointer, array, and slice indexing aligned and avoids implicit width/sign behavior.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the unsafe-pointer ADR and current grammar.

summary: Raw pointer indexing initially lowered directly to unchecked C indexing with no bounds or runtime helper checks.
evidence_paraphrase: The finalized May contract selected direct unchecked lowering and excluded bounds checks and runtime helpers.
alternatives: Validate every pointer access at runtime | Use a dedicated runtime pointer-index helper
rationale: At the time, unsafe func made the author solely responsible for provenance and range, matching direct C behavior.
adr_recommendation: The superseding checked-by-default runtime contract is directly covered by Dea-wide ADR-0010.

summary: Raw pointer index reads and writes evaluate side-effectful base and index operands exactly once.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan promotes existing single-evaluation lowering behavior to the pointer-index language contract.
alternatives: Permit backend duplication of base or index evaluation | Forbid side effects in indexing operands
rationale: Indexing must not duplicate observable effects merely because an lvalue requires address materialization.
adr_recommendation: Extend ADR-0010 with the single-evaluation semantic guarantee; a separate ADR is not needed.

summary: A runtime extern pointer parameter is nullable in Dea when the runtime already defines null as a non-panicking, non-UB sentinel outcome.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan widens only functions whose C implementation already handles NULL with a defined sentinel and excludes panic or UB cases.
alternatives: Keep all FFI pointer parameters non-null regardless of runtime behavior | Make every raw-pointer FFI parameter nullable
rationale: The Dea signature should expose the actual runtime contract without claiming safety for functions whose null behavior panics or invokes C undefined behavior.
adr_recommendation: No standalone ADR is warranted for this narrow signature correction; keep the rule and exact outcomes in the normative stdlib inventories.

summary: Shared specialized container types and entry types use Type1Type2Container ordering.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan normalizes the remaining public outliers to StringVector, StringStringLinearMap, IntStringLinearMap, and correspondingly ordered entry names.
alternatives: Use ContainerType or ContainerKeyValue ordering | Permit each specialized container family to choose its own order
rationale: A single parameter-before-container convention makes specialized public types predictable across L0 and L1.
adr_recommendation: P2: record shared specialized-stdlib type and helper naming in a compact cross-level stdlib API naming ADR.

summary: The specialized container renames are hard renames with no compatibility aliases or mixed-name transition period.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly excludes aliases and any old/new transition while preserving behavior and ABI outside the source names.
alternatives: Retain aliases for old public names | Deprecate old names over a transition release
rationale: Before a stable compatibility promise, one clean public vocabulary avoids permanently carrying duplicate specialized APIs.
adr_recommendation: P2: bundle with the proposed shared stdlib API naming and breaking-rename policy ADR.

summary: Fixed-size arrays are first-class value types spelled T[N], with the element type and length both part of type identity.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan chooses T[N] and states that both T and N are encoded in the type.
alternatives: Make arrays reference types | Erase N from type identity and use a runtime-length container
rationale: A statically sized value type gives deterministic layout, copy, and ownership behavior for the first array primitive.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the fixed-size array ADR.

summary: Pointer and array suffix order is source-significant: T*[N] is an array of pointers and T[N]* is a pointer to an array.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan assigns different type meanings to pointer-before-array and array-before-pointer suffixes.
alternatives: Normalize pointer/array suffix order | Use parentheses or prefix syntax to distinguish the constructions
rationale: Source-order composition makes each suffix a predictable type constructor and preserves distinct storage shapes.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the array-policy and ordered-suffix ADRs.

summary: A fixed-array length must resolve to a positive compile-time int value that fits the L1 int range.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan rejects zero, negative, malformed, and out-of-int-range lengths and stores a concrete length in the semantic type.
alternatives: Allow zero-length fixed arrays | Use a wider or implementation-defined host size domain
rationale: Positive int-sized dimensions keep layout concrete and make runtime index comparison use the language's canonical integer type.
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0011 as amended by the compile-time constant-value ADR.

summary: The initial fixed-array grammar allowed only integer literals as array lengths.
evidence_paraphrase: The original semantic array type took integer-literal metadata and rejected nonliteral lengths.
alternatives: Accept named compile-time constants from the start | Accept arbitrary constant expressions
rationale: Literal-only bounds minimized the initial parser and constant-evaluation surface while arrays were bootstrapped.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: The current broader constant-expression rule is covered by ADR-0016; no historical ADR is warranted.

summary: Adjacent array dimensions follow C-like source order and contiguous row-major layout.
secondary_categories: ABI and linking | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: The plan defines int[2][3] as two rows of three ints stored contiguously in row-major order.
alternatives: Interpret the leftmost dimension as innermost | Lower multidimensional arrays as nested wrapper objects
rationale: C-like order and layout make generated storage predictable and interoperable with the C backend.

summary: Array literals use bracket syntax and require a known contextual fixed-array target; bare literals have no standalone type.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects [a, b] literals but rejects them when no T[N] target supplies element type and capacity.
alternatives: Infer an array type and length from every bare literal | Require an explicit T[N](...) constructor for all array values
rationale: Contextual typing avoids an implicit length/type inference policy while retaining concise initialization.

summary: Short contextual array literals default-initialize omitted trailing elements, [] means all-default, and overlong literals are rejected.
evidence_paraphrase: The literal contract permits zero through N explicit values, fills the remainder deterministically, and forbids values beyond N.
alternatives: Require exactly N explicit elements | Leave omitted elements uninitialized | Truncate excess elements
rationale: Deterministic padding gives safe concise initialization without introducing uninitialized storage or silent data loss.

summary: Safe L1 array declarations must use initialized let syntax; bare uninitialized array declarations are illegal.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan keeps the existing initialized declaration form so safe code cannot observe uninitialized array storage.
alternatives: Allow let a: T[N]; with uninitialized elements | Permit uninitialized arrays only in unsafe functions
rationale: Every array value begins in a deterministic valid state, including elements with ownership obligations.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the fixed-array value and initialization policy in ADR-0011.

summary: Array constructor syntax is T[N](arg), with exactly one literal or element-typed fill argument; an array-valued element may be broadcast across an outer dimension.
evidence_paraphrase: The sole constructor argument is either a contextual literal or one value of the element type, including an inner array value for multidimensional broadcast.
alternatives: Use a comma-separated positional constructor | Allow arbitrary constructor arity | Disallow multidimensional row broadcast
rationale: One constructor form covers explicit prefix initialization and uniform fill without introducing general type-as-call construction.

summary: new T[N] allocates zero/default-initialized array wrapper storage and returns T[N]*; initialized allocation mirrors value-constructor rules.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan extends new to arrays with zeroed storage and the same literal/fill initialization semantics as stack values.
alternatives: Support arrays only as stack/value objects | Return a dynamic-array reference rather than T[N]* | Leave heap array storage uninitialized
rationale: Heap arrays retain the same fixed type and initialization guarantees as value arrays while using existing new/drop ownership.
adr_recommendation: Extend ADR-0011 with heap new/drop array semantics; no separate ADR is needed.

summary: Each fixed-array instantiation lowers to a deterministic generated C wrapper struct containing one data[N] field.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects a wrapper-struct representation for every concrete array type.
alternatives: Lower array values directly as anonymous C arrays | Use pointer-plus-length descriptors | Generate nested wrapper fields for every dimension
rationale: A named wrapper makes arrays passable and returnable as C values while preserving deterministic structural identity.
adr_recommendation: P1: add or extend an ADR for fixed-array C representation and FFI/ABI exposure, including wrapper layout and deterministic names.

summary: Fixed-array reads and writes check bounds before access and route failures through _rt_panic_oob(index, length).
secondary_categories: Language semantics | Backend and C emission
evidence_section: Implementation Phases / Phase 5: Bounds-checked indexing and runtime support
evidence_paraphrase: Both arr[i] and arr[i] = value test the index before .data[index] and call the shared out-of-bounds panic helper on failure.
alternatives: Use unchecked C array indexing | Check only writes | Inline a host abort rather than use a shared runtime failure path
rationale: A shared checked access path preserves the no-undefined-behavior contract and gives every generated array access one runtime failure boundary.

summary: Fixed-array index operations evaluate their base and index expressions exactly once.
evidence_paraphrase: The array indexing contract couples bounds checking with single evaluation of both operands.
alternatives: Permit checks/lowering to duplicate operand evaluation | Forbid side effects in array-index operands
rationale: Safety checks must not change observable program behavior by repeating side effects.

summary: Arrays recursively participate in ARC copy, assignment, cleanup, element replacement, and heap drop using retain-before-release and reverse cleanup rules.
evidence_section: Implementation Phases / Phase 6: Recursive ARC and heap arrays
evidence_paraphrase: Managed elements are recursively retained and released, cleanup walks backward, assignment is alias-safe, slot replacement reuses ordinary rules, and drop cleans before free.
alternatives: Forbid ARC-bearing array element types | Make arrays shallow-copy unmanaged aggregates | Require manual element cleanup
rationale: A value array must preserve the ownership semantics of its element type in every copy and destruction path.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the Dea-wide ARC model and the fixed-array ADR.

summary: C FFI exposure of fixed arrays uses the same wrapper-struct representation rather than a slice or raw-buffer convention.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly chooses wrapper-struct exposure and defers any C-facing slice/buffer policy.
alternatives: Expose fixed arrays as T* plus length | Define a separate C-facing slice ABI | Forbid fixed arrays at extern boundaries
rationale: Using the value representation avoids inventing a second array ABI before a general C buffer policy exists.
adr_recommendation: P1: include the array extern/FFI boundary in the proposed fixed-array representation ADR.

summary: L1 type suffixes are semantic unary constructors applied left-to-right in source order.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan replaces fixed pointer-depth/nullable metadata with an ordered constructor rule.
alternatives: Normalize suffixes into a fixed pointer-then-nullable shape | Apply suffixes right-to-left | Require parentheses for every mixed suffix form
rationale: Each written suffix applies to the type already constructed on its left, preserving a predictable and extensible type grammar.

summary: Nested optional types are not collapsed; T?? preserves distinct outer and inner absence states.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan assigns T?? three observable states rather than normalizing it to T?.
alternatives: Collapse Optional(Optional(T)) to Optional(T) | Reject repeated nullable suffixes
rationale: Every constructor application retains its own semantic information and storage state.

summary: The null-pointer niche is used only for the immediate shape Optional(Pointer(T)); outer optional layers use explicit wrappers.
evidence_paraphrase: T*? may use NULL directly, but T*?? needs an outer wrapper to distinguish outer absence from an inner null pointer.
alternatives: Collapse every nullable pointer nesting into one NULL niche | Never niche-optimize nullable pointers
rationale: The immediate niche remains compact without erasing distinct nested optional states.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0012 and normative backend documentation.

summary: T?* is a valid pointer to optional-T storage and remains distinct from T*?.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan admits pointer-to-optional because optional values are first-class storage values.
alternatives: Reject pointers to optional storage | Normalize T?* to nullable pointer T*?
rationale: First-class optional values can occupy addressable storage just like other value types.

summary: void* remains valid, but void? and void?* are rejected because optional void is not a value object.
evidence_paraphrase: Ordered suffixes do not make void itself nullable or storable, although a pointer to void remains a valid raw pointer type.
alternatives: Allow optional void as a unit-like value | Reject void* together with other void suffix forms
rationale: Pointer-to-void has an FFI role, whereas optional void would invent value semantics for the no-value type.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0012 and the grammar.

summary: The canonical parsed and semantic type representation is a recursive constructor tree, not base-name metadata plus pointer depth and a nullable flag.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan makes the ordered suffix list canonical in the AST and pointer/optional recursive constructors canonical in semantic types.
alternatives: Keep pointer_depth and is_nullable as the canonical representation | Add ad hoc fields for every new suffix kind
rationale: Recursive constructors preserve arbitrary ordering and allow arrays and future suffix forms to compose without lossy overlays.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0012 at the semantic level; the internal representation is a consequence and needs no separate ADR.

summary: The L1 binary interface uses one end-to-end recursive mangling grammar rather than separate link-name and type-component schemes.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan collapses the compatibility scaffold into one recursive encoding for every LBI-mangled entity before the first stable release.
alternatives: Keep a broad link-name layer separate from type encodings | Use unrelated manglers for values and types
rationale: One grammar is self-describing, uniformly extensible, and avoids parallel naming rules with no binary compatibility need.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the LBI symbol-mangling ADR.

summary: LBI terminals use N for values, S for structs, E for enums, and I for compiler infrastructure/lifecycle symbols.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan assigns entity-kind sigils that match the recursive type grammar and retains I for non-source infrastructure.
alternatives: Keep broad S for every source entity | Use distinct value sigils for functions, let, and const
rationale: The terminal identifies the entity namespace while preserving one compact single-letter grammar.
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0008 and the normative ABI specification.

summary: An LBI function symbol appends its complete function type component to the value terminal.
evidence_paraphrase: Functions use N<name> followed by arity, parameter, and result encodings rather than a name-only broad-S link name.
alternatives: Mangle functions by module and name only | Store the signature solely in interface metadata
rationale: The static linker can detect signature mismatches and distinguish future overloads without consulting a sidecar file.

summary: LBI names for plain let and const bindings omit their types.
evidence_paraphrase: Bindings use N<name> with no trailing type component because they cannot be overloaded.
alternatives: Encode every binding's type in its symbol | Use different terminals for let and const
rationale: A type suffix adds name length without disambiguation value while interface fingerprints cover surface compatibility.

summary: Unsafe function signatures carry the X type modifier in LBI names, so safe/unsafe mismatch is a link error.
secondary_categories: Type system | Ownership and memory safety
evidence_paraphrase: The trailing function component includes X for unsafe signatures even though C function-pointer shapes remain compatible.
alternatives: Erase unsafe from mangled names | Use a different terminal namespace for unsafe functions
rationale: Link identity preserves the L1 type distinction across separately compiled modules and blocks silent C-level type punning.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the LBI and unsafe-marker ADRs.

summary: The pre-release LBI migration was one atomic break with no dual emission, dual demangling, or version-negotiation period.
evidence_paraphrase: Because L1 had no shipped binaries, the plan deliberately rejects every compatibility bridge during the scheme change.
alternatives: Emit old and new names in parallel | Add mangling-version negotiation | Retain a dual demangler during migration
rationale: A pre-stable one-shot break avoided permanent ABI complexity whose only purpose would have been compatibility with unshipped artifacts.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: The surviving unified scheme is covered by ADR-0008; the completed migration policy needs no separate ADR.

summary: A source main function receives ordinary signature-bearing LBI mangling; a compiler-generated entry shim calls that mangled symbol.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan gives main no mangling exception and keeps host entry adaptation in a generated shim.
alternatives: Expose source main directly as the host C main symbol | Give source main a special name-only LBI encoding
rationale: User main remains an ordinary module function while process entry concerns stay in compiler infrastructure.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the LBI and per-module lifecycle ADRs.

summary: The shared integer-helper module is named std.integer, while floating-point helpers remain in the separate L1 std.real module.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects std.integer for the integer surface and preserves std.real as the distinct floating-point module.
alternatives: Keep the broader std.math name | Merge integer and floating-point helpers into one module | Rename both numeric modules
rationale: The module identity accurately reflects its integer-only responsibility and leaves real-number APIs in their established domain.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the stdlib module-boundaries ADR.

summary: The std.math to std.integer change is a hard source-level rename with no compatibility module, alias import, or transition shim.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan keeps helper behavior stable but deliberately removes every active compatibility path for the old module identity.
alternatives: Retain std.math as an alias module | Deprecate std.math through a transition release
rationale: A clean pre-stable source break prevents two canonical identities for the same integer API and keeps LBI/module examples unambiguous.
adr_recommendation: P2: bundle this with sys.memory and container renames in a shared stdlib API compatibility and hard-rename policy ADR.

summary: T[] is a first-class non-owning slice descriptor copied by value as {int len; T* data} with no retain, release, cleanup, or ownership transfer.
secondary_categories: Type system | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: The plan chooses a two-field non-owning descriptor whose ordinary value copies do not affect the lifetime of underlying storage.
alternatives: Make slices owning reference-counted buffers | Represent slices as raw pointers without length | Use a borrow-checked reference type
rationale: A small descriptor supplies variable-length views without committing L1 to ownership transfer or lifetime inference.

summary: T[_] is reserved for future language use and is rejected rather than interpreted as a slice.
evidence_paraphrase: The inferred-length-looking suffix is explicitly kept distinct from the empty-bracket slice suffix.
alternatives: Use T[_] as the slice spelling | Assign T[_] inferred fixed-array length semantics immediately
rationale: Reserving the spelling avoids accidentally freezing semantics for a future inferred-length array feature.

summary: Without lifetime analysis, slices are limited to locals, parameters, and call arguments and are rejected in returns and long-lived storage.
evidence_paraphrase: The accepted lifetime model excludes return types/expressions, struct fields, top-level lets, and heap payload fields.
alternatives: Allow general slice escape without analysis | Reject slices as stored locals and parameters too | Introduce borrow/lifetime checking first
rationale: Conservative escape restrictions keep every view within the evident lifetime of its owning fixed-array storage.

summary: The compiler-owned L1 len intrinsic returns int.
evidence_paraphrase: The initial len contract includes both owning fixed arrays and non-owning slices and fixes the result type to int.
alternatives: Expose length only as methods or fields | Return an unsigned or size-specific integer
rationale: One prelude operation gives both statically and dynamically sized contiguous values a common length query in the canonical integer domain.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the prelude and slice ADRs.
reviewer_notes: The independently superseded operand-domain restriction is recorded by B04-DEC-072.

summary: The initial len intrinsic accepted only fixed arrays and slices, excluding strings and every other operand type.
evidence_paraphrase: The word only made the initial operand domain closed over the two newly related aggregate/view types.
alternatives: Include string length from the start | Use an extensible protocol for len
rationale: The first tranche scoped len narrowly to the array/slice feature under implementation.
adr_recommendation: Update ADR-0015 to reflect the current broadened string operand; no new ADR is required.

summary: slice accepts only fixed arrays and slices and has one-, two-, and three-argument forms.
evidence_paraphrase: The source value, optional start, and optional third argument define exactly three accepted arities over arrays or slices.
alternatives: Provide separate full-slice and subslice operations | Accept raw pointer operands | Use a variadic intrinsic
rationale: One bounded intrinsic covers whole views and subranges without inventing pointer-to-slice conversion.

summary: The third slice argument denotes a count, not an exclusive end index.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly resolves the common start/count versus start/end alternative in favor of count.
alternatives: Interpret the third argument as an exclusive end index | Offer distinct start-count and start-end overloads
rationale: Start plus count directly describes the resulting descriptor length and makes zero-length ranges explicit.

summary: Slice indexing performs a bounds check before any generated C pointer dereference.
secondary_categories: Language semantics | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: The plan makes pre-dereference bounds validation part of every slice index access.
alternatives: Use unchecked pointer indexing | Check only in debug builds | Return an optional element
rationale: A safe view must validate its dynamic length before touching the backing storage.

summary: A zero-length slice result is canonically represented with len = 0 and data = NULL.
secondary_categories: Language semantics | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects a normalized null data pointer for every empty result rather than retaining an arbitrary one-past or backing pointer.
alternatives: Preserve the original data pointer when count is zero | Use a non-null sentinel pointer
rationale: Canonical empties avoid meaningless pointer arithmetic state and make descriptor behavior deterministic.

summary: Implicit T[N] to T[] conversion occurs only when a slice target is already known: arguments, annotated local initialization, or assignment to a slice variable.
secondary_categories: Ownership and memory safety | Language semantics
evidence_paraphrase: The plan defines three contextual conversion sites and excludes unconstrained C-style array decay.
alternatives: Decay every fixed array expression to a slice | Require explicit slice(...) conversion everywhere
rationale: Known-target conversion is ergonomic at API boundaries while keeping ownership and value identity explicit elsewhere.

summary: Raw pointer operands are rejected by slice; L1 has no pointer-to-slice conversion in this surface.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly excludes raw pointers and declines to infer a length or ownership boundary from them.
alternatives: Accept pointer plus inferred or separate length | Allow unsafe pointer-to-slice conversion
rationale: A raw pointer alone supplies neither a valid extent nor a lifetime guarantee for a safe slice descriptor.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0015 and the current slice operand contract.

summary: The initial slice type surface supports T[], T*[], and T?[] but rejects T[]? and T[]* to preserve escape restrictions.
secondary_categories: Ownership and memory safety | Language syntax
evidence_paraphrase: Element pointer/optional shapes are admitted, while nullable-slice and pointer-to-slice outer suffixes are excluded from the first lifetime model.
alternatives: Allow every ordered suffix around slices | Support only plain T[] elements
rationale: Rich element types remain useful without introducing outer slice indirections that could bypass the conservative escape boundary.

summary: The LBI type component for a slice is the single-letter recursive form W<element>.
evidence_paraphrase: W is fixed before implementation as a non-owning window marker distinct from nominal struct S.
alternatives: Reuse S for slice descriptors | Use a multi-letter Slice marker | Choose a different one-letter sigil
rationale: W follows the single-letter recursive LBI rule and gives structural slice types a stable non-nominal identity.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the LBI and slice ADRs.

summary: The compiler-owned virtual dea prelude exports len and slice intrinsics; ordinary prelude shadowing and qualified dea:: access apply.
evidence_paraphrase: The new intrinsics reuse the virtual module's ordinary shadowing and qualified escape-hatch rules.
alternatives: Reserve len and slice as keywords | Make unqualified intrinsic names override user declarations | Place them in a physical std module
rationale: Compiler-owned operations remain in the normal module/name-resolution system without confiscating common user identifiers.
adr_recommendation: Covered by the virtual-prelude and slice ADRs.
reviewer_notes: This wording isolates the novel architectural placement of len/slice from shadowing behavior already settled by the virtual-prelude plan.

summary: Slice range construction validates start and count before pointer arithmetic or dereference and reuses _rt_panic_oob on failure.
evidence_paraphrase: Generated slicing checks the complete range first and shares the existing array out-of-bounds runtime failure path.
alternatives: Form a pointer first and validate afterward | Use unchecked C pointer arithmetic | Add a distinct slice-range panic ABI
rationale: Pre-arithmetic validation avoids undefined pointer formation and keeps array, slice-index, and slice-range failures on one runtime contract.
adr_recommendation: Covered by ADR-0015 and the shared out-of-bounds helper decision in ADR-0011.

summary: Repeating the same open import emits exactly one non-fatal RES-0036 warning at the redundant import.
evidence_paraphrase: Both L0 stages detect a duplicate module name and reuse L1's single-warning code, message, and source location.
alternatives: Silently accept duplicate imports | Emit one ambiguity warning per imported symbol | Make duplicate imports fatal
rationale: Redundancy is useful to flag, but it does not make the program semantically ambiguous.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: ADR not warranted for this narrow diagnostic contract

summary: Opening the same module repeatedly is semantically idempotent: the resolver skips the redundant merge and leaves the first import's visible symbols usable.
evidence_paraphrase: Duplicate detection occurs before export merging, and the repeated open is skipped instead of turning identical symbols into ambiguity.
alternatives: Merge the exports again and diagnose each collision | Remove duplicated names from the visible set | Treat repeated opens as fatal
rationale: Reopening the same module introduces no second semantic origin and therefore must not corrupt name resolution.
adr_recommendation: A narrow resolver idempotence correction belongs in module-system reference documentation and tests.
reviewer_notes: Duplicate-open idempotence is durable but too narrow and obvious to justify an ADR.

summary: An orphaned parent-owned statement keyword is diagnosed as unmatched (`else` without `if`, `cleanup` without `with`) rather than as a generic expression error.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan assigns shared parent-specific diagnostics only after the owning statement parser has had the chance to consume the keyword.
alternatives: Keep generic unexpected-expression diagnostics | Treat the keyword as a top-level recovery token
rationale: The parser has enough structural knowledge to report the actual unmatched construct consistently across stages.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: ADR not warranted beyond the shared catalog

summary: A failed statement parse is synchronized and resumed inside its current block instead of unwinding the function and restarting top-level parsing mid-body.
evidence_paraphrase: The self-hosted block parser null-checks each statement, invokes statement synchronization, and continues with forward-progress guards.
alternatives: Abort the entire block on the first statement error | Propagate failure to top-level recovery
rationale: Block-local recovery prevents unrelated valid body statements from being misdiagnosed as top-level tokens.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: shared parser recovery and phase-boundary contract

summary: The canonical case default-arm spelling is `_ => Stmt`, aligning case with match.
evidence_paraphrase: Phase 1 selects the wildcard plus match-arrow spelling as canonical and deliberately gives it an arrow.
alternatives: Continue using else as the canonical default | Introduce a new default keyword | Require a block-only default arm
rationale: The spelling removes dangling-else ambiguity and reuses the existing match wildcard/token vocabulary.

summary: During Phase 1, the legacy `else` case default remains accepted but emits warning PAR-0242.
evidence_paraphrase: The migration preserves legacy parsing as a warning-producing compatibility path rather than removing it immediately.
alternatives: Remove else in one flag-day change | Accept else indefinitely without warning
rationale: The staged migration keeps existing code compiling while making the replacement visible.

summary: While the legacy case-default `else` remains, an unbraced value-arm `if` followed by ambiguous `else` is rejected with PAR-0243.
evidence_paraphrase: The one grammar configuration that could silently change meaning becomes a hard error, with bracing or `_ =>` as repairs.
alternatives: Always bind else to the nearest if without a diagnostic | Always treat it as the case default | Disallow unbraced if arm bodies
rationale: Ambiguity must not silently select a different program meaning during the compatibility phase.

summary: L1 case arm values use the same type-comparability model as `==` rather than requiring exact literal/scrutinee type equality.
evidence_paraphrase: Case dispatch adopts equality comparability while retaining compile-time safety.
alternatives: Require exact type equality | Apply implicit assignment conversion rules | Permit arbitrary comparable expressions
rationale: A case literal denotes a value comparison, so ordinary equality is the coherent semantic oracle.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: L1 case value comparability and lowering

summary: L1 case scrutinees support builtin integer families, float, double, bool, and string, with corresponding literal arm families; other type families remain excluded.
evidence_paraphrase: The parser adds real literals and semantic checking defines the accepted builtin scrutinee/literal domains.
alternatives: Keep int/byte/bool/string only | Permit enums, pointers, nullable, aggregates, and arbitrary expressions
rationale: The selected families have existing value-equality semantics that can be lowered without new pattern machinery.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: L1 case value comparability and lowering

summary: A well-formed integer case arm outside the scrutinee's value domain remains valid but emits an always-false warning instead of an error.
evidence_paraphrase: The classifier separates possible, always-false, and incomparable arms and gives impossible integer values warning-only semantics.
alternatives: Reject out-of-domain values as errors | Silently accept without warning | Narrow or wrap the arm value
rationale: The arm is well-typed but cannot match; a warning communicates that fact without turning it into a compatibility-breaking error.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: L1 case value comparability and lowering
