summary: The backend uses C switch only when every arm is a safe C case label semantically identical to L1 equality; converted, real, string, or always-false cases lower as equality chains.
evidence_paraphrase: Unsafe or conversion-dependent dispatch avoids C case labels and uses if/else equality lowering.
alternatives: Always lower case as C switch | Always lower every case as if/else | Emit narrowing casts in case labels
rationale: Backend selection must preserve Dea equality and avoid C overflow, undefined behavior, or runtime checked arithmetic in labels.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: L1 case value comparability and lowering

summary: The body of an always-false case arm is still type-checked, so local source errors are not hidden by reachability classification.
evidence_paraphrase: Always-false arms remain syntactically valid and their bodies receive ordinary type checking.
alternatives: Skip semantic checking for unreachable arm bodies | Reject the arm before checking its body | Downgrade all body errors to warnings
rationale: Compile-time unreachability affects flow, not the requirement that every source branch be well typed.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: L1 case value comparability and lowering

summary: L1 Phase 2 accepts only `_ =>` as a case default; `else` is an unmatched else (PAR-0123), and transitional PAR-0242/PAR-0243 behavior is removed.
evidence_paraphrase: The L1 parser deletes the else-default branch and dangling-else guard, leaving the terminal wildcard-only grammar.
alternatives: Retain the deprecated spelling indefinitely | Remove wildcard and return to else | Require braced case arms
rationale: Once `_ =>` is the sole default token sequence, the dangling-else ambiguity disappears entirely.

summary: An unreleased language level may intentionally advance a grammar migration before L0, with diagnostic-parity skips documenting the forward-only divergence from the L0 oracle.
secondary_categories: Bootstrap and self-hosting | Diagnostics and recovery
evidence_section: Context / Why this is safe before the L0 plan
evidence_paraphrase: L1 lands Phase 2 first and records PAR-0242/PAR-0243 as intentional skipped oracle cases while L0 remains checked.
alternatives: Require lockstep grammar migrations across all levels | Treat every oracle divergence as a parity failure
rationale: Level independence permits forward evolution while explicit skips distinguish intended divergence from accidental drift.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: intentional cross-level divergence and parity-exception policy
reviewer_notes: Intentional parity exceptions govern oracle relationships and cross-level bootstrap evolution.

summary: Invalid break or continue outside a loop reports its placement error but does not make the following statement unreachable; valid loop control still does.
evidence_paraphrase: Reachability state changes only after placement validation succeeds, including inside with headers and inline cleanup.
alternatives: Treat any syntactic break/continue as terminating flow even when invalid | Suppress all reachability warnings after errors
rationale: An invalid control transfer has no semantic target and therefore cannot justify a derived unreachable-state fact.
adr_recommendation: Keep in analyzer tests and reference flow notes

summary: An opening brace is a statement synchronization boundary and must not be consumed while recovering from the preceding malformed statement.
evidence_paraphrase: All frontends stop statement synchronization at `{`, preserving the matching block structure.
alternatives: Skip `{` while searching for a semicolon or keyword | Abort the enclosing block on the preceding error
rationale: Consuming an opening brace unbalances nesting and causes cascading top-level diagnostics.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P1 ADR: shared parser recovery and phase-boundary contract

summary: Canonical Dea source text is UTF-8; invalid UTF-8 is rejected during source decoding, and optional BOM stripping remains a level-local compiler-contract detail.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan identifies UTF-8 decoding plus optional BOM stripping as the existing source contract and deliberately preserves it.
alternatives: Treat source as arbitrary bytes | Adopt a locale-dependent encoding | Require or forbid BOM globally
rationale: A single portable encoding separates decoding validity from grammar vocabulary.

summary: Unicode text is permitted in comments and string literal payloads even though the language vocabulary is restricted.
evidence_paraphrase: The Stage 1 correction preserves UTF-8 source and Unicode content inside comments and strings.
alternatives: Restrict all source characters to ASCII | Allow Unicode only through escapes
rationale: Natural-language text and data do not require Unicode-sensitive identifier semantics.

summary: Identifiers, module-name components, keywords, builtin type names, and other grammar-defined vocabulary are ASCII-only.
evidence_paraphrase: Explicit ASCII predicates replace host-language Unicode identifier classes while Unicode comment/string text stays valid.
alternatives: Unicode identifiers and module names | Host-language-specific Unicode character classes
rationale: ASCII vocabulary keeps token classification and module identity deterministic across bootstrap implementations.

summary: Invalid source characters are consumed as recoverable lexical errors and scanning continues so one pass can identify later invalid characters.
evidence_paraphrase: All lexer implementations loop, consume an invalid character, record LEX-0040, and resume at the next valid token.
alternatives: Abort tokenization at the first invalid character | Use recursive recovery
rationale: Iterative recovery reports multiple lexical faults without recursion limits.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
adr_recommendation: Covered by the successor recovery ADR

summary: Recovered tokenization initially stops at a pre-parser phase gate whenever any lexer error exists.
evidence_paraphrase: The first recovery design returns accumulated lexer errors and deliberately does not enter parsing.
alternatives: Carry lexer recovery information into the parser | Parse the raw recovered stream without a token-level error contract
rationale: The initial gate avoided misleading parser cascades from an underspecified recovered stream.

summary: The first missing statement-block close at EOF puts the parser in a terminal aborted state, emits PAR-0091 once, stops every recovery loop, and still returns its partial module.
evidence_paraphrase: A shared parser-state flag makes EOF terminal across block, synchronization, and top-level loops while preserving partial results.
alternatives: Emit one missing-close diagnostic per unclosed nesting level | Deduplicate PAR-0091 after parsing | Throw a stage-specific fatal exception
rationale: Once EOF prevents a block close, nested recovery cannot gain new source information and should not repeat the same error.
adr_recommendation: Keep as a documented parser recovery invariant

summary: Recoverable lexer diagnostics are deferred into dedicated wrapper tokens carrying their code, message, and full source span.
evidence_paraphrase: The lexer encapsulates recoverable errors in token-stream objects instead of emitting them immediately.
alternatives: Emit diagnostics directly from the lexer | Use an out-of-band side list disconnected from token positions
rationale: Token-attached diagnostics preserve exact physical spans and a parser-visible recovery point.

summary: Lexer recovery parity is defined as a shared logical-token contract; each frontend may use a different physical wrapper layout.
secondary_categories: Diagnostics and recovery | Bootstrap and self-hosting
evidence_paraphrase: Python may group diagnostics on one wrapper while native stages may queue multiple wrappers ending in one recovered logical token.
alternatives: Require byte-identical token data structures across stages | Allow each frontend to expose unrelated recovery behavior
rationale: Observable parser recovery can remain equivalent without forcing host-language-inappropriate representation.

summary: Parser token access is logical: it emits each wrapped lexer diagnostic exactly once despite backtracking, skips wrappers without recovery, and exposes the recovered token when present.
evidence_paraphrase: Wrapper interpretation is centralized at parser token access with idempotent emission.
alternatives: Make each parse routine handle wrapper tokens | Permit duplicate emissions on backtracking | Expose wrappers as ordinary grammar tokens
rationale: One logical-token chokepoint keeps recovery transparent to grammar code and stable under lookahead.

summary: The parser always runs after recoverable lexing errors; only later semantic and code-generation phases remain gated by accumulated errors.
evidence_paraphrase: The post-lexing barrier is removed while downstream error gates remain.
alternatives: Stop before parsing on every lexer error | Continue through semantic analysis using placeholders
rationale: Parsing malformed files preserves AST shape and later syntax diagnostics for editor workflows without permitting erroneous code generation.

summary: Malformed recoverable literal and numeric diagnostics preserve a reasonable parser-visible placeholder or valid-prefix token through the wrapper stream.
evidence_paraphrase: String, byte, integer, real, and escape faults use code-specific recovered token shapes rather than discarding the whole literal position.
alternatives: Skip every malformed literal entirely | Abort parsing on literal errors | Invent one universal placeholder token
rationale: A token in the expected grammatical family preserves useful parse shape while later phases remain blocked.

summary: LEX-0040 groups one contiguous invalid-character run in a no-recovery wrapper that the parser skips logically.
evidence_paraphrase: Invalid characters have no meaningful grammar token, so a whole contiguous run is represented once and skipped.
alternatives: Emit one wrapper per byte or code point | Synthesize an identifier or punctuation token
rationale: Grouping avoids diagnostic noise while refusing to fabricate a misleading grammar token.

summary: An unterminated block comment remains an unrecoverable trivia error with no parser-visible recovery token.
evidence_paraphrase: LEX-0070 stays on its direct no-recovery path because a block comment is trivia and consumes to EOF.
alternatives: Wrap it as a recovered comment token | Synthesize a comment terminator
rationale: There is no following meaningful token position to recover once the unterminated comment consumes the remaining file.

summary: Native lexer diagnostic columns count Unicode code points while source offsets remain byte-based; display width is out of scope.
evidence_paraphrase: Native byte lexers advance columns only on non-continuation UTF-8 bytes, matching the Python oracle.
alternatives: Count UTF-8 bytes | Count grapheme clusters | Count terminal display cells
rationale: Code-point columns give deterministic cross-stage positions while retaining efficient byte offsets.

summary: Token-dump modes expose physical lexer-error wrappers and their recovery tokens but do not emit the deferred diagnostics.
evidence_paraphrase: The token dump renders wrapper structure while diagnostic emission remains owned by the parser, which dump mode does not run.
alternatives: Render only logical recovered tokens | Emit diagnostics as a side effect of token dumping
rationale: The inspection surface shows the physical token model without violating single-emission routing.

summary: The .l1m module-interface artifact is deterministic human-readable text rather than a binary arena dump.
evidence_paraphrase: The interface is a language-facing textual artifact.
alternatives: Binary serialized compiler state

summary: Every .l1m file begins with module interface <name>;.
evidence_paraphrase: The artifact carries an explicit canonical module identity header.

summary: The .l1m grammar reserves a fingerprint string field while hash semantics are defined separately.
evidence_paraphrase: Artifact shape and fingerprint policy are separate architectural responsibilities.

summary: Exported transparent structs and enums are serialized structurally so importers can reconstruct layout.
evidence_paraphrase: The initial interface artifact carries public nominal layout.
alternatives: Opaque names only

summary: Exported functions appear in .l1m as declarations ending in semicolons and never include bodies.
evidence_paraphrase: Interfaces expose callable signatures but no implementation.

summary: Exported const declarations inline literal values in .l1m.
evidence_paraphrase: Compile-time constant values are part of the consumer-visible interface.
alternatives: Type-only const records

summary: Exported let declarations carry types but not initializer values in .l1m.
evidence_paraphrase: Runtime storage is exposed by type only.
alternatives: Serialize let initializer expressions

summary: Interface emission order is canonical and independent of source declaration order.
evidence_paraphrase: Equivalent semantic surfaces produce deterministic text.
alternatives: Preserve source declaration order

summary: The source export manifest is omitted from .l1m; only the effective exported declarations are serialized.
evidence_paraphrase: Different source manifest spellings with the same public surface produce byte-identical interface text.
alternatives: Serialize export syntax verbatim

summary: Stage 1 parses .l1m in a constrained mode that accepts only interface constructs.
evidence_paraphrase: Interface replay does not reuse unrestricted source parsing.
alternatives: Parse interfaces as ordinary source modules

summary: -c <module> and --compile <module> are the stable compile-only CLI spellings.
evidence_paraphrase: All current compiler stages reserve the conventional compile-only mode spelling.
alternatives: Retain -c as host-C selection

summary: -I <dir> and --interface-path <dir> define the interface search path for compile-involving flows.
evidence_paraphrase: The conventional include-style short option is reassigned to module interfaces.
alternatives: Use -I for runtime headers | Long option only

summary: Runtime include and library paths keep long options but move their short aliases from -I/-L to -Ri/-Rl.
evidence_paraphrase: The coordinated L0/L1 migration frees conventional linker and interface option spellings.
alternatives: Keep historical -I and -L meanings

summary: Dea-specific controls use semantic short namespaces, while conventional -g, -S, -L, and -l stay reserved until their normal capabilities land.
evidence_paraphrase: The CLI avoids assigning conventional compiler/linker flags unrelated meanings.
alternatives: Reuse conventional flags for Dea-specific controls

summary: The compiler driver owns import-closure and build-graph computation rather than delegating it to scripts.
evidence_paraphrase: Dependency orchestration remains a compiler responsibility.
alternatives: External build scripts compute module closure

summary: Semantic analysis and C generation can consume a supplied direct-provider .l1m without loading provider source.
evidence_paraphrase: Direct interface replay establishes the source-independent consumer pipeline.
alternatives: Always reparse provider source

summary: Interface replay preserves transparent nominal layout and keeps opaque imported nominals layout-hidden and pointer-only.
evidence_paraphrase: Consumer capabilities follow the visibility state encoded by the provider interface.
alternatives: Materialize all provider layouts | Treat every nominal as opaque

summary: Only interfaces selected by source imports are activated for semantic replay.
evidence_paraphrase: Supplied-but-unimported interfaces do not inject symbols.
alternatives: Activate every supplied interface
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Dropping an imported opaque pointee is rejected because hidden owned fields require provider-side cleanup.
evidence_paraphrase: Layout hiding also hides the information required for consumer-side destruction.
alternatives: Generate incomplete consumer cleanup

summary: Source resolution searches system roots before project roots and preserves declaration order within each group.
evidence_section: Phase 2: CLI option and mode design (completed 2026-07-16)
evidence_paraphrase: Search precedence is deterministic across root classes and stable within a class.
alternatives: Project roots before system roots | Filesystem order
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
reviewer_notes: The cited lines distinguish ordered -I storage from the existing system-before-project source resolver. The frozen summary incorrectly labeled the latter as interface-search precedence.

summary: L1 opacity is a derived state of layout-hiding field visibility rather than a distinct type-system primitive.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan adopts the ADR's layout-hiding model and derives opacity from the no-visible-fields endpoint.
alternatives: Make opaque a separate type-system kind | Use name hiding only while exposing layout | Gate opaque handles behind unsafe
rationale: Deriving opacity from visibility makes interface projection and allowed operations follow one rule.

summary: A public pointer type `U*` may cross an exported surface only when `U`'s nominal name is explicitly exported, opaque or transparent.
evidence_paraphrase: The exported-surface rule accepts pointers at an opaque frontier but rejects pointers to unexported names.
alternatives: Allow inference-only pointers to unexported types | Require pointees to be fully transparent
rationale: A consumer can name and carry an opaque handle without needing its layout, but no undeclared type may leak into an interface.

summary: A type used by value in an exported signature or visible aggregate field must be transparent; opaque and unexported by-value types are rejected.
evidence_paraphrase: The exported-surface rule independently distinguishes layout-requiring by-value use from pointer use.
alternatives: Permit sized opaque by-value use | Emit private layout implicitly | Allow unsafe by-value opaque use
rationale: Separate compilation cannot represent or manipulate a by-value type whose layout is absent from the interface.

summary: Transparent aggregate exports require a transparent by-value layout closure, while pointer fields stop traversal at an exported nominal frontier.
evidence_paraphrase: The checker follows by-value field edges and stops at pointer pointees after verifying name visibility.
alternatives: Check only direct field names | Recursively require pointer pointees to be transparent | Allow unexported intermediaries
rationale: One-level enforcement composes transitively and makes every emitted transparent layout self-contained.

summary: An `.l1m` interface projects opaque types as explicit name-only declarations and transparent types as full definitions.
evidence_paraphrase: Opaque structs/enums round-trip as bodyless opaque declarations; ordinary bodyless nominal declarations are invalid.
alternatives: Omit opaque names entirely | Emit full hidden layouts | Use an out-of-band interface visibility table only
rationale: The interface is self-contained while exposing exactly the layout authorized by the export surface.

summary: The implemented visibility model supports only transparent and fully opaque endpoints; mixed or partial field visibility is rejected pending a later offset-versus-accessor decision.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan explicitly rejects the partially visible middle rung rather than silently assigning it an ABI.
alternatives: Expose selected field offsets | Generate accessor thunks | Support declaration-site field visibility immediately
rationale: Partial visibility would prematurely fix ABI layout/accessor policy that the endpoint model does not need.

summary: Enum visibility is all-or-none: per-variant visibility is not part of the opaque-export model.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan deliberately keeps enums at transparent-all-variants or opaque-no-variants endpoints.
alternatives: Export selected variants | Hide payload layout while exposing tags
rationale: Variants determine enum layout and construction/matching surface, so the first model keeps them coherent as a unit.

summary: The grouped source form `export opaque { T, ... }` exports nominal names while hiding all of their fields or variants.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects grouped export-opaque syntax as sugar for the fully layout-hidden visibility endpoint.
alternatives: Attach opaque to each type declaration | Use `export T hiding { ... }` | Infer opacity from pointer-only use
rationale: The grouped manifest spelling makes name export deliberate while preserving ordinary transparent `export T` behavior.

summary: Importers may name, hold, pass, and return pointers to an opaque nominal, but operations requiring its hidden layout—field access, dereference, construction, allocation, or by-value use—are rejected.
evidence_paraphrase: Opaque pointer round trips work across modules, while imported field access, construction, allocation, and by-value use fail.
alternatives: Make opaque names entirely unusable to consumers | Permit unsafe layout access | Expose size and alignment as a sized-opaque middle state
rationale: Opaque pointers support safe handle APIs without exposing or inventing a consumer-side representation.

summary: Fixed-array-bound source syntax accepts integer literals plus visible local or qualified `const` references.
evidence_paraphrase: The direct array-bound grammar grows from integer literals to identifiers and qualified identifiers naming visible constants.
alternatives: Require integer literals only | Accept arbitrary expressions directly in the bound grammar | Accept only unqualified constant names
rationale: Named bounds improve maintainability while the existing positive-int semantic constraint continues to determine array layout.

summary: Case-arm value syntax accepts the existing literals plus visible local or qualified `const` references.
evidence_paraphrase: The direct case-value grammar grows to identifiers and qualified identifiers while existing semantic comparability rules remain in force.
alternatives: Keep literal-only case arms | Accept arbitrary runtime expressions | Accept only unqualified constant names
rationale: Named constants compose with equality-based case semantics without admitting runtime-dependent arm expressions.

summary: L1 defines separate constant-expression domains for array bounds, case arms, const initializers, and serialized interface constants instead of one universal constexpr rule.
evidence_paraphrase: The design explicitly assigns different accepted value domains to four constant contexts.
alternatives: Use one undifferentiated constexpr grammar and semantic domain | Permit everything accepted by const initializers in every constant context
rationale: Each consumer has distinct layout, comparability, and serialization constraints.

summary: One reusable semantic `ConstValue` evaluator resolves literals and visible local or qualified const references for every constant-value consumer.
evidence_paraphrase: A shared evaluator entry point recursively resolves the literal and const-reference subset instead of duplicating logic by context.
alternatives: Implement context-specific literal/name evaluators | Let each backend interpret const syntax independently | Forbid const-to-const references
rationale: One evaluator gives all consumers consistent values and creates an extensible boundary for later operators.

summary: Array bounds are resolved to concrete numeric lengths before semantic types, generated ABI, and `.l1m` signatures; symbolic bound names are not preserved there.
secondary_categories: Type system | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: Interfaces emit a resolved numeric length such as string[25], not the source constant name string[NUM_LANG].
alternatives: Preserve symbolic bound expressions in interfaces | Defer bound resolution until C emission | Represent variable-length ABI arrays
rationale: Concrete lengths keep type identity, layout, and separately compiled interfaces deterministic.

summary: Duplicate case-arm detection compares evaluated constant values, so distinct constant names denoting the same value conflict.
evidence_paraphrase: The checker extends duplicate-arm rejection to const-evaluated values rather than comparing source spelling or symbol identity.
alternatives: Treat different constant names as distinct arms | Detect duplicates only among literals | Permit duplicates and select the first arm
rationale: Case dispatch depends on runtime value equality, not the provenance or spelling of the arm value.

summary: Direct or indirect cycles among compile-time const references are rejected with a semantic cycle diagnostic.
evidence_paraphrase: Recursive const-reference evaluation tracks active definitions and treats A-to-B-to-A recursion as SIG-0201 rather than a value.
alternatives: Forbid every const-to-const reference | Accept cycles with an implementation-defined value | Fail with the generic non-constant diagnostic only
rationale: Recursive references need a deterministic invalid-program rule and must not recurse indefinitely in the compiler.

summary: Compile-time casts cover every L1 integer family and require exact target-range validity; out-of-range values are rejected rather than wrapped.
evidence_paraphrase: The selected integer targets span tiny through ulong and use TYP-0700 instead of wraparound.
alternatives: Permit only int casts | Use modular narrowing semantics | Forbid casts in const expressions
rationale: Compile-time conversion must agree with checked integer semantics and produce one exact target value.

summary: Compile-time real casts support only `float` to/from `double`; integer-to-real and real-to-integer casts remain outside the const-expression subset.
evidence_paraphrase: The real conversion domain is deliberately limited to float/double conversion and excludes integer/real crossings.
alternatives: Support every runtime numeric cast at compile time | Support no real casts | Permit only widening float-to-double casts
rationale: The narrow subset reuses established real-literal representation without settling broader compile-time numeric conversion policy.

summary: Compile-time bool and string casts are identity-only.
evidence_paraphrase: The selected scalar subset permits bool-to-bool and string-to-string casts but no conversion between those families.
alternatives: Permit truthiness conversions to bool | Permit compile-time stringification | Exclude bool and string casts entirely
rationale: Identity casts preserve type-directed source forms without inventing new compile-time conversions.

summary: Exported cast constants serialize in `.l1m` as folded target-typed literals rather than preserving cast expression syntax.
secondary_categories: Backend and C emission | CLI and distribution
evidence_paraphrase: The interface artifact records the result value and target type, not the source cast AST.
alternatives: Preserve cast expressions in module interfaces | Reject exported constants initialized by casts | Serialize compiler-private constant bytecode
rationale: Value serialization keeps interface consumers independent of evaluator syntax and implementation details.

summary: Nullable, pointer, and aggregate casts are excluded from L1's compile-time constant-expression subset.
evidence_paraphrase: The cast tranche explicitly leaves nullable, pointer, and aggregate conversions for future work.
alternatives: Mirror every runtime cast in constant evaluation | Admit null-pointer constants only | Allow aggregate reinterpretation during compilation
rationale: The first const-cast surface remains scalar and avoids defining compile-time pointer identity, nullability, or aggregate conversion semantics.

summary: For initialization and update headers retain ordinary abrupt simple statements—return, break, continue, and drop—rather than being restricted to non-abrupt BasicStmt forms.
evidence_paraphrase: The final grammar keeps non-declaration simple statements in both header positions and explicitly rejects the proposed ban on abrupt statements.
alternatives: Restrict headers to assignment and expression statements | Allow only expressions in update position
rationale: The language keeps one coherent simple-statement surface and defines control-flow behavior instead of banning it.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P0 ADR: for-header control flow, liveness, and cleanup semantics

summary: A for initialization may declare a local, but the update clause rejects declarations: `let` uses PAR-0145 and L1 local `const` uses PAR-0263.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan preserves update-only declaration rejection while leaving the initialization on the broader SimpleStmt grammar.
alternatives: Permit declarations in both header positions | Reject declarations in both header positions
rationale: Initialization creates loop-scoped bindings; repeated update execution does not create a new declaration scope each iteration.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P0 ADR: for-header control flow, liveness, and cleanup semantics

summary: Break and continue executed in a for initialization or update clause target the enclosing loop context, not the loop whose header is still being executed; absent an enclosing loop they are invalid.
secondary_categories: Semantic analysis | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: Both header execution points are explicitly outside the inner loop's active control context.
alternatives: Target the for loop being initialized or updated | Ban loop control in headers
rationale: The inner loop cannot receive control before initialization or after update has already entered its own continuation path.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P0 ADR: for-header control flow, liveness, and cleanup semantics

summary: For executes initialization once before the inner loop is active; update runs after body fallthrough or an inner-body continue and before the next condition check.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan fixes the runtime order and the destination of body-level continue.
alternatives: Check the condition before initialization | Skip update after continue | Run update after the next condition
rationale: A single explicit ordering eliminates self-looping update-continue behavior and stage divergence.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P0 ADR: for-header control flow, liveness, and cleanup semantics

summary: For-loop definite liveness assumes the body may execute zero times; a binding is usable only if alive on every path reaching the use.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects conservative all-path liveness with a zero-iteration path.
alternatives: Assume one iteration for liveness | Treat any backedge assignment as reviving a binding after the loop
rationale: A condition may be false initially, so body-only effects cannot establish post-loop safety.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P0 ADR: definite drop-liveness and loop fixed points

summary: Assignment to a dropped bare local revives the binding only after the right-hand side has been validated and evaluated.
evidence_paraphrase: Bare-target revival is delayed so `p = p` cannot use the destination's newly revived state to validate its own RHS.
alternatives: Revive at assignment entry | Never allow reassignment to revive a dropped local
rationale: Fresh assignment can restore liveness, but the old dead value cannot be read to construct that assignment.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P0 ADR: definite drop-liveness and loop fixed points

summary: A definite return from for initialization contributes to function definite-return analysis, but returns in the body or update do not because the loop may execute zero times.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan propagates guaranteed initialization returns but refuses to treat zero-iteration regions as guaranteed.
alternatives: Ignore every header return in definite-return analysis | Treat body/update returns as guaranteed
rationale: Initialization always executes, while body and update execution depend on the condition and control path.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P0 ADR: for-header control flow, liveness, and cleanup semantics

summary: Definite-return analysis recognizes returns from established `with` header, inline-cleanup, cleanup-block, and body forms while honoring cleanup's ability to replace a pending exit.
secondary_categories: Language semantics | Ownership and memory safety
evidence_paraphrase: The analyzer propagates definite returns from all established with forms according to the existing pending-exit and cleanup-precedence semantics.
alternatives: Ignore returns originating in with headers or cleanup | Always preserve the pending exit even when cleanup exits abruptly | Treat any syntactic return inside with as definite
rationale: Definite-return facts must reflect the actual cleanup-mediated control transfer rather than the source position of a return statement.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P0 ADR: shared for-header flow, liveness, and cleanup semantics

summary: Compile-time arithmetic and unary negation are limited to checked Dea 32-bit `int` payloads; bigint, real, string, aggregate, pointer, and nullable arithmetic remain unsupported.
evidence_paraphrase: The arithmetic tranche deliberately selects checked 32-bit int operations and defers every broader value family.
alternatives: Use arbitrary-precision compile-time arithmetic | Fold every runtime numeric operator | Keep const initializers literal-and-cast only
rationale: A bounded evaluator can mirror existing int runtime rules without prematurely defining general constexpr behavior.

summary: Compile-time bitwise and shift operators accept only non-negative 32-bit `int` payloads, and bitwise complement remains bounded by the same domain.
evidence_paraphrase: Bitwise &, |, ^, shifts, and complement use a deliberately narrower non-negative bounded-int policy.
alternatives: Apply signed two's-complement bitwise semantics | Use arbitrary-precision bitwise values | Exclude all bitwise const folding
rationale: The restriction avoids host-dependent signed representations and unbounded complement values.

summary: Compile-time `&&` and `||` use short-circuit evaluation, so an unreachable non-constant or invalid operand does not invalidate the constant initializer.
evidence_paraphrase: The evaluator deliberately skips unreachable boolean operands and diagnoses only reachable invalid ones.
alternatives: Eagerly evaluate both operands | Reject boolean operators in const initializers | Suppress errors in all operands after one constant side
rationale: Compile-time evaluation must preserve the language's runtime short-circuit semantics.

summary: The scalar constant subset folds unary logical not over supported boolean values.
evidence_paraphrase: Unary ! is one of the shipped constant-expression operators.
alternatives: Limit constant booleans to literals | Defer unary logical operations | Treat ! as runtime-only
rationale: Logical negation lets compile-time booleans compose without expanding into general constexpr execution.

summary: Overflow, invalid shifts, divide/modulo by zero, unsupported value families, and reachable non-constant operands make a const expression non-evaluable and diagnostic-producing rather than causing a compiler failure.
evidence_paraphrase: Invalid and unsupported operations remain ordinary non-evaluable constant inputs, never internal compiler failures.
alternatives: Adopt host arithmetic behavior | Treat invalid constant operations as compiler panics | Wrap overflow and continue
rationale: User source errors need deterministic language diagnostics and must not escape into implementation failure modes.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Accepted scalar const expressions serialize in `.l1m` as folded literals; source expression syntax is not preserved.
evidence_paraphrase: Module interfaces consume the evaluator's folded value instead of carrying expression syntax.
alternatives: Serialize expression trees in interfaces | Reject exported constants with nonliteral source initializers | Serialize compiler-private evaluator bytecode
rationale: Canonical literal output gives separately compiled consumers a stable value contract without embedding evaluator semantics in artifacts.

summary: A visible top-level const bool determines `if`, `while`, and `for` liveness, but a shadowing local binding keeps the condition dynamic.
secondary_categories: Language semantics | Ownership and memory safety
evidence_paraphrase: Flow analysis consumes known top-level const booleans while respecting lexical shadowing as a runtime value.
alternatives: Ignore named constants in liveness | Treat any same-spelled local as the top-level constant | Fold only literal conditions
rationale: Flow facts follow resolved symbols and values, not token spelling, and improve definite-return and ownership analysis.

summary: Branches proven dead by constant-boolean flow still undergo ordinary type checking; only impossible liveness paths are removed.
evidence_paraphrase: Constant flow suppresses impossible reachability effects but does not turn dead branches into unchecked source.
alternatives: Skip all semantic analysis of dead branches | Report all liveness effects as though both branches execute | Reject dead branches outright
rationale: Static validity remains independent of runtime reachability while ownership and definite-return facts use known control flow.

summary: The scalar constant subset folds equality and ordering comparisons over supported scalar values.
evidence_paraphrase: Scalar equality and comparison are independently included in the shipped bounded evaluator.
alternatives: Fold equality but not ordering | Defer all comparison folding | Allow comparison of unsupported aggregate or pointer values
rationale: Comparison-produced booleans let named constants participate coherently in flow analysis and other constant contexts.

summary: L1 keeps the per-site pointer-check fast path `static inline` in its public runtime header while exporting slow-path and string-tracking helpers through both normal and traced archive manifests.
evidence_paraphrase: The hot cache lookup remains header-inline, while miss handling and tracking helpers are archive symbols in both runtime variants.
alternatives: Put every check behind an archive call | Inline the entire tracker implementation in the public header | Expose helpers only in the normal archive
rationale: This split preserves call-site caching performance and L1's archive-based runtime ABI across traced and untraced builds.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: L0 and L1 editor tooling is maintained in one shared repository package under `editors/`.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selects one editors tree for both language levels instead of separate packages.
alternatives: Separate repositories per level | Separate in-repository packages with duplicated infrastructure
rationale: The language levels share enough syntax and tooling infrastructure that one package avoids drift and duplication.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P2 ADR: editor integration architecture and public identities

summary: The baseline editor stack is syntax and navigation tooling—TextMate, Tree-sitter, Vim/Emacs fallbacks, and Ctags—while LSP and semantic services are deferred.
evidence_paraphrase: The first supported stack is native grammar/index support; diagnostics, completion, hover, navigation semantics, and compiler JSON belong to a later plan.
alternatives: Start with an LSP | Piggyback on C highlighting only | Ship only a VS Code grammar
rationale: Useful cross-editor support can ship without prematurely defining a compiler service protocol.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P2 ADR: editor integration architecture and public identities

summary: The single Tree-sitter grammar is named `dea`, parses the error-tolerant L1 syntactic superset, and relies on separate host mappings for L0 versus L1.
evidence_paraphrase: Tree-sitter uses L1 as the richer structural grammar while level identities remain distinct outside the parser.
alternatives: Maintain separate L0 and L1 parsers | Parse only the L0 common subset | Make the structural grammar reject incomplete input
rationale: One superset parser supports both levels and interactive editing without duplicating closely related grammar implementations.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P2 ADR: editor integration architecture and public identities

summary: The compiler remains the semantic authority; editor grammars must be conservative, error-tolerant structural tools rather than semantic validators.
evidence_paraphrase: Editor grammars structure incomplete code and intentionally do not encode type checking or level-specific semantic rejection.
alternatives: Treat Tree-sitter acceptance as language validity | Duplicate compiler semantic checks in editor regexes
rationale: Only compiler phases have the context and normative contracts needed to validate Dea semantics.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P2 ADR: editor integration architecture and public identities
reviewer_notes: This settles the authority boundary between compiler frontend semantics and permissive editor parsers.

summary: Editor hosts expose L0 and L1 as distinct language identities, scopes, filetypes, and extension mappings even though their tooling package is shared.
evidence_paraphrase: The shared package assigns separate dea-l0/dea-l1 IDs, source scopes, Vim filetypes, and .l0/.l1 mappings.
alternatives: Expose one undifferentiated Dea language identity | Ship independent packages to obtain distinct identities | Treat L1 files as L0 plus syntax errors
rationale: Host-visible separation preserves correct level-specific keyword and extension behavior without duplicating the package.
adr_recommendation: Candidate P2 ADR: editor integration architecture and public identities

summary: Generated Dea pointer dereferences, pointer field accesses, pointer indexing, and generated drop cleanup are runtime-validated by default before storage is touched.
evidence_paraphrase: Invalid accesses become Dea runtime diagnostics instead of C undefined behavior, with checked builds as the default.
alternatives: Trust all generated C pointer operations | Require a borrow checker before permitting pointers | Make validation opt-in
rationale: Runtime checking closes aliasing gaps that the current static drop-liveness analysis cannot see.

summary: Pointer validation is backed by allocation records carrying base, extent, alignment, generation, state, memory kind, source sites, and a reserved type identity.
evidence_paraphrase: The address-only tracker is replaced by a provenance-rich allocation record model.
alternatives: Track only live base addresses | Embed metadata immediately beside every allocation | Tag pointer values
rationale: Spatial, temporal, provenance, and diagnostic checks need more than address membership.

summary: Allocation records reserve a type-id field, but runtime type-compatibility enforcement is deferred to a future type-identity initiative.
evidence_paraphrase: The tracker stores type_id without using it in the shipped access checks.
alternatives: Enforce runtime pointee type identity immediately | Omit any type identity hook permanently
rationale: The access-validation tranche can deliver spatial and bounded temporal safety without preempting a broader type-identity design.

summary: The checked tracker covers `new` plus raw allocation, reallocation, free, and drop entry points rather than validating only generated object allocation.
evidence_paraphrase: new, rt_alloc, rt_calloc, rt_realloc, rt_free, and drop all participate in tracker state and validation.
alternatives: Track only new/drop | Track only generated dereferences and ignore raw allocation APIs
rationale: Pointers from stdlib containers and raw memory helpers must share the same validity model as object pointers.

summary: Generated drop is a begin/finish protocol: exact-base validity is established before owned-field cleanup, and the allocation is quarantined only after cleanup completes.
evidence_paraphrase: Drop validation and state transition bracket compiler-generated field cleanup.
alternatives: Mark memory freed before field cleanup | Validate only in the final free helper | Let generated cleanup dereference before validating the base
rationale: Invalid casts and stale drops must fail before cleanup dereferences fields, while valid owned fields remain live during cleanup.

summary: Released blocks remain in a bounded quarantine; temporal-error detection is guaranteed only while a record remains retained, with pointer tagging excluded.
evidence_paraphrase: The design chooses bounded historical retention and explicitly disclaims complete detection after eviction/address reuse.
alternatives: Unbounded tombstones | Immediate record removal | Generation-tagged pointer values
rationale: A bounded quarantine catches common stale aliases without changing pointer representation or leaking unbounded memory.

summary: Memory tracing remains lifecycle-oriented: allocation/free/new/drop events stay visible, but successful access checks, derived validation, and quarantine eviction do not emit trace lines.
evidence_paraphrase: Pointer validation deliberately preserves the existing trace surface instead of adding per-access noise.
alternatives: Trace every checked pointer access | Hide drop lifecycle behind the checker | Create a separate access-trace stream
rationale: Existing ownership traces remain stable and useful without overwhelming output on hot paths.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Every generated checked-access site owns a static cache of its last allocation record and generation; misses use the full tracker and refill it.
evidence_paraphrase: A site-local generation/range fast path avoids hashing on repeated accesses.
alternatives: Full tracker lookup on every access | One global last-record cache | Whole-program static check elision only
rationale: Per-site locality keeps checked mode practical without weakening validation.

summary: Runtime helpers that derive interior pointers validate them against the owning allocation range instead of registering a separate derived-pointer record per call.
evidence_paraphrase: Derived validity follows the owner record's range and temporal state.
alternatives: Register each derived pointer as its own allocation record | Leave helper-derived pointers unchecked
rationale: Owner-based validation preserves temporal detection without unbounded metadata churn for indexing helpers.

summary: Heap string blocks are initially registered eagerly at allocation, while static string spans are registered lazily when raw bytes are exposed.
evidence_paraphrase: The first implementation distinguishes eager heap-ARC tracking from lazy static-span tracking.
alternatives: Register both kinds lazily at exposure | Track every static literal at program startup | Never validate string byte pointers
rationale: Eager heap registration initially tied tracker lifetime directly to ARC allocation/release.
adr_recommendation: Historical predecessor retained in ADR plan history

summary: Heap and static string storage exposed as raw bytes is tracked read-only: checked reads succeed and checked writes fail before mutation.
evidence_paraphrase: Both ARC-managed and static string spans reject write-mode checked access.
alternatives: Permit raw mutation of string bytes | Return copied mutable buffers | Disallow any raw byte view
rationale: Raw views remain compatible with immutable string value semantics.

summary: ARC-managed and static tracked storage cannot be released through drop, rt_free, or rt_realloc.
evidence_paraphrase: Runtime-managed record kinds reject ownership operations from raw/object allocation families.
alternatives: Allow raw free of ARC string storage | Treat every tracked allocation family as interchangeable
rationale: The operation that owns a lifetime must remain the only operation authorized to end it.

summary: Checked validation is the default, but compile-time unchecked defines remove validation, tracking, and quarantine without changing generated C shape.
secondary_categories: Ownership and memory safety | Backend and C emission
evidence_paraphrase: L0_RT_UNCHECKED and DEA_RT_UNCHECKED select an explicit performance opt-out at C/runtime build time.
alternatives: Always require checks | Generate different C in checked and release modes | Make unchecked the default
rationale: The release escape hatch preserves raw-pointer performance while keeping one backend output contract.

summary: Pointer-safety semantics are shared across levels, but each level may retain its existing runtime layout, naming, and header-versus-archive boundary.
secondary_categories: Bootstrap and self-hosting | ABI and linking
evidence_paraphrase: The shared contract is ported mechanically without forcing already-divergent runtime representations to converge.
alternatives: Require one physically identical runtime implementation | Permit semantic divergence between level runtimes
rationale: L0's header runtime and L1's archive runtime can expose the same safety behavior through appropriate local ABI shapes.

summary: Output and link-facing flags follow the generated C input so object and archive link order stays stable.
evidence_paraphrase: All levels keep output and linker flags, including runtime and sys.real libraries, after the generated input.
alternatives: Move all flags before the input

summary: Allocation-tracker and quarantine constants are compile-time override points in both runtimes.
evidence_paraphrase: Four tracker/quarantine constants gain guarded definitions so builds can tune them.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: The prebuilt L1 archive runtime reads quarantine byte and record overrides once at first tracker use.
evidence_paraphrase: Because an archive cannot be rebuilt per application, L1 accepts one-time environment overrides.
alternatives: Require archive recompilation | Read the environment on every operation

summary: Heap strings enter the pointer tracker lazily at first raw-byte exposure rather than at allocation.
evidence_paraphrase: String allocation stops registering eagerly; rt_string_bytes_ptr performs idempotent registration and release tolerates never-registered storage.
alternatives: Register every heap string eagerly

summary: The first lazy-registration design tracked the whole string allocation at its header base, making the exposed bytes an interior pointer.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan selected the heap block base and header-plus-bytes extent so the returned byte pointer resolved through interior containment.
alternatives: Track the exposed byte pointer as the exact base

summary: `--unchecked` is a first-class mode flag for build, run, and generated-C operations.
evidence_paraphrase: The driver surface admits unchecked only in build, run, and gen.
alternatives: Keep unchecked accessible only through raw C defines

summary: Unchecked mode is mutually exclusive with ARC or memory tracing, and no traced-unchecked runtime variant exists.
evidence_paraphrase: Trace modes require checked-runtime invariants, so unchecked and tracing cannot be combined.
alternatives: Ship a traced-unchecked variant

summary: L1 links a dedicated unchecked runtime archive or TinyCC object set that matches the generated unchecked prelude.
evidence_paraphrase: Mode defines remove inline checks; the L1 driver selects libdea_rt_unchecked.a or its TinyCC object variant.
alternatives: Use one runtime archive for both checked and unchecked generated code

summary: The unchecked runtime preserves the full public runtime symbol surface as pass-through stubs so mixed generated-code/runtime variants remain link-compatible.
evidence_paraphrase: Checked generated code can link an unchecked archive and unchecked generated code can link a checked archive.
alternatives: Remove check symbols from the unchecked ABI
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Native compiler executables initially remained fully checked but used a 256-record quarantine, while generated programs and L1 archives retained the 4096 default.
evidence_paraphrase: The compiler-only profile changed retention but not full checked validation.
alternatives: Use the same 4096-record default everywhere | Use unchecked compiler executables

summary: Explicit C defines and runtime tuning variables take precedence over compiler-build quarantine defaults.
evidence_paraphrase: The helper preserves explicit user control and applies its compiler default only when no higher-priority setting exists.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: `unsafe func` is a source-level proof boundary independent of optional checked-runtime validation.
evidence_paraphrase: Checked builds may dynamically validate unsafe pointer operations, while unchecked builds lower them directly; neither changes the source contract.
alternatives: Define unsafe solely as a runtime-mode switch

summary: `--check-basic` is a first-class checked mode for build, run, and generated-C operations.
evidence_paraphrase: All three compilers accept the mode in build, run, and gen and emit the level-specific basic define.
alternatives: Expose basic checks only through raw C defines

summary: Basic mode is mutually exclusive with unchecked and trace modes, with no traced-basic archive.
evidence_paraphrase: The mode matrix rejects basic plus unchecked or tracing, and runtime macros reject basic plus unchecked.
alternatives: Ship traced-basic | Permit conflicting mode defines

summary: Basic checked mode retains exact-base validation, quarantine, generation caches, read-only exact-base protection, and alignment checks while omitting treap containment and spatial checks for hash misses.
evidence_paraphrase: Hash hits preserve full checked behavior; misses receive only alignment/overflow handling and interior pointers are not contained through the treap.
alternatives: Full checked treap validation | Completely unchecked access

summary: L0 realizes basic checks through a generated prelude define, while L1 selects a dedicated basic archive or TinyCC object variant.
evidence_paraphrase: The two runtime shapes implement one shared mode through level-appropriate build boundaries.

summary: Darwin arm64 compiler executables retain UUID and ad-hoc signature commands, while only non-executable comparison copies neutralize UUID payloads.
evidence_paraphrase: Executable loader metadata is preserved; normalization is confined to byte-comparison copies.
alternatives: Disable UUID/signature generation on arm64 | Ignore native bootstrap identity

summary: Tracked allocations carry distinct raw, new, ARC, static, and foreign provenance; drop accepts only new storage, while free and realloc accept only raw storage.
evidence_paraphrase: The runtime splits allocation families and makes their release operations non-interchangeable.
alternatives: Treat raw and new allocations as one releasable kind

summary: Generated drop uses a sized begin/finish ABI that validates expected pointee size and alignment before cleanup; no unsized compatibility entry point remains.
evidence_paraphrase: The unreleased ABI changes atomically to a sized begin/finish protocol and removes obsolete unsized helpers.
alternatives: Keep an unsized compatibility wrapper | Validate only base provenance

summary: Heap-string tracking is based at the exact exposed byte pointer so basic-mode writes see a read-only exact-base record.
evidence_paraphrase: The plan replaces header-base interior tracking with byte-base exact tracking.
alternatives: Track the allocation header base and rely on interior lookup

summary: Foreign memory enters checked pointer validation only through explicit register and unregister operations that record lifetime and extent without transferring ownership.
evidence_paraphrase: rt_register_foreign supplies extent/read-only state; unregister invalidates tracking without freeing the payload.
alternatives: Treat all unregistered extern pointers as permanently valid | Transfer ownership to the Dea runtime

summary: Identical live foreign registrations are idempotent, conflicting registrations panic, and unregistration never frees foreign storage.
evidence_paraphrase: The foreign registration API defines repeat, conflict, and release semantics explicitly.

summary: Unchecked mode validates foreign-registration arguments but intentionally records no tracker state.
evidence_paraphrase: Unchecked remains an explicit validation opt-out while retaining basic API argument checks.
alternatives: Track foreign lifetimes even in unchecked mode | Skip registration argument validation

summary: Darwin arm64 bootstrap executables retain Mach-O UUID and ad-hoc signature load commands, while Intel Darwin keeps the existing linker normalization.

alternatives: Disable UUID/signatures on every Darwin architecture

summary: Repository review and organization requests are read-only, while a draft request authorizes only the named draft.

summary: A local implementation or commit never authorizes a push; every push requires an explicit user request.
evidence_paraphrase: Local finalization and remote mutation are separate authorization tiers.

summary: Public, cross-repository, workflow-dispatching, and deployment-triggering writes require fresh confirmation immediately before execution with exact target and downstream effects.
evidence_paraphrase: High-risk remote writes add a just-in-time disclosure and confirmation gate.

summary: A public branch push is permitted only to the exact designated branch already configured as the checked-out branch's upstream; refspec and upstream overrides cannot bypass the gate.
evidence_paraphrase: The public destination must be repository-designated and already tracked.
alternatives: Permit ad-hoc HEAD refspecs | Change upstream as part of publication

summary: Creating a release tag requires an explicit request naming both tag and target.
evidence_paraphrase: A plan mentioning a tag does not satisfy the separate tag-creation gate.
alternatives: Treat implementation of a release plan as tag authority

summary: Pushing a release tag has its own fresh confirmation gate listing the remote and every known automatic publication effect.
evidence_paraphrase: Tag creation and tag publication are two independently authorized operations.

summary: Plans, sandbox approvals, tool approvals, CI, and agent review grant no remote or publication authority.
evidence_paraphrase: Technical capability and successful validation cannot satisfy a user authorization gate.

summary: Each external repository owns its publication workflow; Dea guidance for blog work is advisory and recommends exact-copy review plus explicit authorization.
evidence_paraphrase: Dea does not claim enforcement authority over independently owned repositories.

summary: Normative Stage 1 compiler diagnostics use a direct, context-free stderr channel independent of operational log thresholds and formatting.
evidence_paraphrase: Compiler diagnostics and operational logging are distinct output contracts; diagnostic rendering cannot acquire timestamps or logger severity prefixes.

summary: `test` is the stable normal validation tier and excludes only the dedicated broad trace sweep; focused trace regressions remain included.
evidence_paraphrase: Root, L0, and L1 expose a normal aggregate without the standalone broad trace runner.
alternatives: Make every local validation run the broad trace sweep

summary: `test-all` is mandatory for trace-sensitive, runtime, memory, ownership, ARC, pointer-validation, emitted-lifetime, mixed, or uncertain changes.
evidence_paraphrase: Trace risk, including uncertainty, selects the full aggregate.
alternatives: Select the tier solely by file type

summary: Native L0 Stage 2 and L1 Stage 1 compiler executables default to basic checks plus a 256-record quarantine, while generated programs and the default L1 archive remain fully checked.
evidence_paraphrase: The compiler-only profile changes to basic plus q256 without weakening generated-program defaults.
alternatives: Full checks plus q256 | Unchecked compiler executables

summary: L1 exposes level-named controls for the L0 runtime embedded in its Stage 1 compiler, separate from generated-program flags and L1 runtime-archive controls.
evidence_paraphrase: Compiler construction, generated program C options, and runtime archives have distinct variable namespaces.
alternatives: Require callers to inject underlying L0 defines through L0_CFLAGS
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Compiler runtime-mode selection gives explicit raw mode defines highest priority, then explicit unchecked/basic variables, with empty mode variables selecting full checks.
evidence_paraphrase: The helper preserves raw flags, resolves level-named selectors, and makes an explicit empty setting the full-check opt-in.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Compiler quarantine limits are selected independently from runtime mode and each explicit limit can override or disable only its corresponding default.
evidence_paraphrase: Byte/count precedence is independent of full/basic/unchecked mode selection.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Interface compatibility is one fingerprint of the canonical effective exported surface, replacing declaration-level hashes.
evidence_paraphrase: The completed tranche chooses a single whole-module compatibility value and removes declaration suffix hashes.
alternatives: Per-symbol hashes | Hash verbatim interface text

summary: LBI fingerprint version 1 uses SipHash-1-3 with public fixed key `DeaL1-fp-v1-key!`, distinct from randomized runtime hashing.
evidence_paraphrase: The algorithm and 16-byte ASCII key are fixed ABI inputs for accidental staleness/corruption detection.
alternatives: Random per-process key | Cryptographic signature

summary: Fingerprint input is a versioned, length-framed UTF-8 byte stream with LF separators, no NUL terminator, and no dependence on rendered prose or host layout.
evidence_paraphrase: The canonicalizer serializes explicit records under the l1-interface-fingerprint-v1 domain.
alternatives: Hash emitted prose | Use platform line endings or in-memory layout

summary: The textual fingerprint is mandatory `sip13:` plus exactly 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits, with no implicit tag or alternate spelling.
evidence_paraphrase: The tagged envelope has exact syntax and distinguishes malformed values from unsupported algorithms.
alternatives: Untagged hexadecimal | Uppercase or variable-width digest

summary: The fingerprint includes exported structs, enums, aliases, functions, consts, and lets, exposing full transparent layouts but only opacity marker and name for opaque nominals.
evidence_paraphrase: Only effective exported declarations participate; module location, dependencies, private implementation, metadata, compiler, time, and host facts are excluded.
alternatives: Hash private implementation details | Hash opaque hidden layouts

summary: Top-level declaration groups and names are canonically sorted, while field, parameter, variant, and other nested semantic orders are preserved.
evidence_paraphrase: Source declaration order does not affect group ordering, but semantically meaningful nested order remains in records.
alternatives: Preserve all source order | Sort semantically ordered members
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: String literals enter fingerprints through one decoded canonical value: scalar escapes become UTF-8 while octal escapes retain raw-byte meaning.
evidence_paraphrase: Producer literal folding consumes the lexer's decoded value rather than a second escape decoder.
alternatives: Hash source spelling | Decode octal escapes as Unicode scalars
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Integer literals enter fingerprints by checked canonical numeric value rather than source base, separators, or spelling.
evidence_paraphrase: Canonicalization bounds typed values, normalizes decimal text, and converts binary/octal/hex payloads deterministically.
alternatives: Hash literal token spelling
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Dependency records retain their syntax but store the provider module's whole fingerprint, and declaration records contain no hash fields or suffixes.
evidence_paraphrase: The model removes per-declaration hashes and renames dependency values to provider_fingerprint.
alternatives: Keep both module and declaration hashes

summary: A module's dependency manifest is excluded from its own fingerprint, so private import changes do not invalidate unchanged downstream public surfaces.
evidence_paraphrase: Provider expectations are compatibility inputs at linking but not part of the consumer's exported-surface digest.
alternatives: Hash require/link manifests into the consumer fingerprint

summary: Consumers validate spelling, recompute the canonical fingerprint, and reject mismatches before normalization, graph registration, name resolution, or semantic replay.
evidence_paraphrase: All filesystem and supplied-interface paths fail closed before semantic use.
alternatives: Trust declared fingerprints | Verify after replay | Fall back to source on mismatch

summary: Version 1 accepts only tagged SipHash-1-3 fingerprints and provides no implicit algorithm or legacy placeholder fallback.
evidence_paraphrase: Malformed and unsupported algorithms receive distinct failures because operational separate compilation had not shipped.
alternatives: Accept legacy empty or untagged values | Infer SipHash for bare hex

summary: The compiler retains the legacy whole-program generator beside one named per-module generator during the separate-compilation transition.
evidence_paraphrase: Callers choose one supported output kind rather than independently toggling emission booleans into hybrid states.
alternatives: Replace build/run atomically before the module ABI exists | Expose combinable emission flags

summary: Per-module output defines exactly one source-backed target module and emits only declarations and required visible type layouts for imported providers.
evidence_paraphrase: Imported definitions cannot leak into the translation unit; transparent required layouts may be reproduced and opaque layouts remain hidden.
alternatives: Emit the whole source closure into every C unit

summary: Compiler-generated per-module lifecycle and entry symbols have external linkage independent of the source export manifest.
evidence_paraphrase: Source export policy controls source symbols but not reserved lifecycle ABI infrastructure.
alternatives: Make lifecycle symbols follow the source export manifest
reviewer_notes: The event's export-external/non-export-static clauses repeat B03-D207 and B03-D208. Only infrastructure linkage is a new atomic choice.

summary: Every module defines an external one-shot `void I4init(void)` that initializes only its own deferred top-level lets and never its dependencies.
evidence_paraphrase: The function exists even when empty; the wrapper owns exactly-once dependency ordering.
alternatives: Emit init only when work exists | Have each module recursively initialize imports

summary: Every module defines an external one-shot `void I4fini(void)` that cleans only its own ARC-managed top-level lets and never its dependencies.
evidence_paraphrase: The function exists even when empty; reverse ordering and exactly-once invocation belong to the wrapper.
alternatives: Use one global finalizer | Have modules recursively finalize imports

summary: A source-backed module emits external `I5entry` only when it defines a resolved zero-parameter non-extern `main`, even when that source main is non-exported.
evidence_paraphrase: The bridge is translation-unit-local access to a possibly static source main; extern declarations alone are ineligible.
alternatives: Require main to be exported | Treat extern main declarations as entry candidates

summary: `I5entry` always returns C `int`: L1 int passes through, bool maps true to 0 and false to 1, and other result types normalize to 0.
evidence_paraphrase: The module bridge preserves the existing process-wrapper result normalization.
alternatives: Expose source result types in the C entry ABI | Reject non-int main results

summary: Per-module output contains no process-level C `main`, dependency lifecycle calls, or argument initialization; a later wrapper owns the complete process sequence.
evidence_paraphrase: Module translation units provide local ABI entry points but do not orchestrate a process.
alternatives: Emit a process wrapper in every entry module | Make I5entry orchestrate lifecycle

summary: A canonical dotted module name maps to a slash-separated relative stem with sibling `.c`, `.o`, and `.l1m` artifacts.

alternatives: Use source paths as artifact stems | Place artifact kinds in separate trees

summary: An explicit compile-only output must be a regular `.o` path, and replacing only its final suffix selects the `.c` and `.l1m` companions.
evidence_paraphrase: Extensionless and directory outputs are rejected rather than guessed.
alternatives: Accept a directory | Infer artifact kind from an extensionless path

summary: Separate-compilation artifact identity depends only on canonical module identity, never source-path spelling, search roots, or import aliases.
evidence_paraphrase: Filesystem and local naming choices cannot create competing artifact identities.
alternatives: Include source-root or alias spelling in identity

summary: The requested compilation target is always source-backed; an interface can satisfy imports but cannot replace the module being compiled.

summary: Imported interfaces are searched in explicit `-I` root order, and the first existing dotted-path `.l1m` candidate wins over source and lower-priority interfaces.

alternatives: Prefer source | Treat multiple matches as ambiguity

summary: A selected interface is authoritative: unreadable, malformed, invalid-UTF-8, or identity-mismatched interfaces fail without source fallback.
evidence_paraphrase: Selection commits to the artifact instead of hiding stale or corrupt interfaces behind available source.
alternatives: Silently fall back to source on any interface failure

summary: Strict interface resolution reports a missing-interface error for every non-virtual imported module.
evidence_paraphrase: MRP_REQUIRE_INTERFACE is the compile-only policy and forbids source fallback.
alternatives: Always allow source fallback
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: When interface resolution permits source fallback and finds no interface, the resolver selects source under the existing source-root precedence and schedules it as a module-graph node.
evidence_paraphrase: MRP_ALLOW_SOURCE_FALLBACK is the build/run fan-out policy when no interface exists.
alternatives: Project roots before system roots | Do not schedule fallback sources
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Compiler-synthesized prelude modules remain virtual and require no `.l1m` or object artifact.

adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: One module-graph node represents one canonical module with exactly one selected source, interface, supplied-registry, or virtual origin.

summary: Source nodes preserve direct imports in exact declaration order, including duplicates and imports used only for side effects.
evidence_paraphrase: The ordered edge sequence is kept independently from deterministic symbol manifests for lifecycle use.
alternatives: Sort/deduplicate all dependency views

summary: Interface `require` denotes a public-surface semantic dependency, while `link` denotes an implementation-only graph obligation that exposes no provider names.
evidence_paraphrase: The two dependency tiers have distinct semantic activation behavior.
alternatives: Activate both tiers semantically | Collapse both tiers into one manifest

summary: The graph recursively closes over providers from both `require` and `link`, but activates only `require` providers for semantic replay.
evidence_paraphrase: Implementation-only providers remain link-set obligations without entering the semantic environment.

summary: Emitted dependency manifests are sorted and deduplicated by provider symbol, and `require` dominates `link` for a symbol present in both.
evidence_paraphrase: Manifest determinism does not overwrite the separately retained direct-import order.

adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Every dependency record naming one provider repeats that provider's whole-module fingerprint; no per-symbol compatibility hash is computed.
evidence_paraphrase: Dependency values are module-level expectations even though records retain provider-symbol syntax.

summary: Source and interface cycles share the complete canonical module-chain diagnostic policy; cache hits are not cycles and failed nodes never become resolved.
evidence_paraphrase: Resolution state distinguishes active recursion, cached success, and terminal failure.
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Semantic types are finalized after source signature resolution so nested wrappers, nominal kinds, and source/interface transparent aliases materialize against the complete provider set.
evidence_paraphrase: A ledger-neutral post-signature pass updates semantic consumers while preserving raw graph and projected interface spelling.
alternatives: Fully materialize parser types before provider signatures exist
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: An interface public surface is valid only against its transitive semantic closure: interface nodes traverse `require`, source nodes traverse direct imports, and `link` never grants surface visibility.
evidence_paraphrase: The analyzer reports RES-0040 when a public type depends only on an implementation-tier link edge.
alternatives: Use the broader link closure for public-surface typing
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Each separately compiled Dea object embeds enough module identity, interface, import, lifecycle, and entry metadata for standalone validation without reopening `.l1m` files.
evidence_paraphrase: Object files become the authoritative standalone-link inputs; metadata-free status is reserved for genuine foreign objects.
alternatives: Reopen sidecar interfaces at link time | Rely on linker symbol failures

summary: Object metadata is emitted as two external C99 `const uint8_t` arrays named by reserved LBI terminals `I8metadata` and `I7imports`.
evidence_paraphrase: Portable compiler-generated arrays carry identity and ordered-import records without custom object sections.
alternatives: Custom object sections | Compiler-specific retention attributes

summary: Both metadata records use a fixed 16-byte little-endian envelope with `DEAL1OBJ` magic, version, record kind, and payload length.
evidence_paraphrase: The common binary header makes record kind and bounded payload size explicit.
alternatives: Native-endian structs | Unversioned byte strings

summary: The identity record contains module name, raw whole-module fingerprint, and the `HAS_ENTRY` flag.
evidence_paraphrase: Version 1 records canonical producer identity and entry candidacy in one payload.

summary: The imports record contains each unique direct non-virtual provider once, in first source-import order, including side-effect-only imports.
evidence_paraphrase: Object metadata preserves module-level provider order and expected fingerprints without per-symbol hashes.
alternatives: Sort providers | Omit side-effect-only imports | Serialize per-symbol compatibility

summary: Metadata format version 1 stores raw SipHash-1-3 digests; supporting another fingerprint algorithm requires a new metadata version.
evidence_paraphrase: The textual algorithm tag is omitted only because the record version fixes its interpretation.
alternatives: Interpret the same version under a new default algorithm | Embed textual tagged values

summary: Both metadata arrays are retained by volatile byte reads from the always-present module `I4init` function.
evidence_paraphrase: A standard-C object reference prevents dead stripping without custom sections or attributes.
alternatives: Custom section retention | Rely on unreferenced external arrays surviving

summary: Object inspection returns exactly one metadata classification: valid Dea metadata, no Dea metadata, or malformed Dea metadata.
evidence_paraphrase: The format-neutral reader separates metadata state from container read failures.
alternatives: Use a binary present/absent result

summary: `NoDeaMetadata` requires a supported relocatable object with neither metadata symbols nor any external normalized `__dea` definition.
evidence_paraphrase: Any incomplete metadata or reserved-LBI evidence is malformed and cannot be reclassified by a foreign-object hint.
alternatives: Treat any object lacking both arrays as foreign | Let caller hints override classification

summary: File access, unsupported-container, and corrupt-container failures remain object-read errors outside the metadata tri-state.
evidence_paraphrase: A container failure never collapses into metadata absence.
alternatives: Treat unreadable or unsupported files as metadata-free
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: L1 inspects relocatable ELF, Mach-O, and PE/COFF files with bounded in-repository readers rather than invoking host tools.
evidence_paraphrase: Readers inspect only bounded section, symbol, and string data and do not load code, apply relocations, or invoke external commands.
alternatives: Shell out to nm or objdump | Depend on platform SDK parsing libraries

summary: Object symbol normalization is format- and architecture-specific and removes only enumerated ABI prefixes, never fuzzy suffixes or arbitrary leading characters.
evidence_paraphrase: ELF, Mach-O, and COFF adapters apply narrowly defined underscore/hash rules for their supported targets.
alternatives: Use fuzzy suffix matching | Strip all leading punctuation
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR

summary: Valid Dea metadata requires identity/import pairing, supported version and flags, canonical consistent identity, lifecycle symbols, and entry-flag agreement.
evidence_paraphrase: Intrinsic object ABI consistency is checked before a module object is accepted.
alternatives: Validate only the byte records and defer symbol consistency

summary: A metadata-free foreign object has no module identity, fingerprint obligation, dependency edge, lifecycle participation, or entry eligibility; process-level C `main` is reported separately.
evidence_paraphrase: Foreign relocatables remain outside the Dea module graph while exposing enough symbol evidence for later link policy.
alternatives: Synthesize module identity for foreign objects | Allow foreign objects into lifecycle ordering
adr_coverage: Covered as part of a broader ADR
